- A-IC3 (2026)
    - title: A-IC3: Learning-Guided Adaptive Inductive Generalization for Hardware Model Checking
    - what: A-IC3 adds an online proof-aware contextual multi-armed bandit to IC3 generalization. A PA-LinUCB agent chooses among static and activity-aware CTG/EXCTG strategies from local CTI and global proof-state features, then updates from clause quality and propagation feedback. The method defines an eight-feature context, push-aware reward, seven arms, and globally fixed hyperparameters, then integrates with rIC3 without offline training. Experiments separate safe/unsafe solving, PAR-2, arm-selection phases, and termination-frame counts; case plots show adaptive choices rather than a fixed arm.

    - what: Reports a Lean4 library for empirical-process learning theory: Gaussian functional inequalities/concentration, covering and chaining culminating in Dudley’s entropy integral, localized least-squares error bounds, linear regression and ℓ1-image covering. Provides a detailed human–AI proof-engineering case study; it does not experimentally establish autonomous research or a causal speedup. Builds coordinate-resampling invariance for heterogeneous independent distributions; Efron–Stein, Rademacher/CLT Gaussian Poincaré, entropy duality/subadditivity, Bernoulli-to-Gaussian log-Sobolev and Herbst concentration. Explicit C1/Sobolev density and mollification handle analytic extension. Dudley uses recursive projections with step distance εk rather than3εk/2, finite-net bounds, a nonnegative shift for Fatou, and separability/path continuity. Covering numbers use WithTop Nat; entropy/integrals have ENNReal canonical versions and real wrappers. Least-squares master theorem exposes sphere nonemptiness, supremum integrability/boundedness and critical-radius hypotheses; ℓ1 covering uses Maurey’s probabilistic finite-net construction. Reported Gaussian concentration is for finite positive dimension, positive Lipschitz constant and threshold under standard product Gaussian measure. Dudley requires σ,D>0, a nonempty totally bounded index set, a pathwise-zero anchor, measurable coordinates, integrable exponential increments, finite entropy integral and continuous sample paths; not arbitrary stochastic processes. The master error theorem assumes f*∈F, star-shaped shifted class, any positive radius satisfying the critical inequality, an ERM for every noise vector, a nonempty sphere at sqrt(tδ), integrable localized absolute suprema at two radii and boundedness. The displayed theorem does not require δ to be the smallest solution. It bounds fixed-design empirical prediction error, not arbitrary population excess risk. Local Gaussian-complexity capacity control additionally assumes total boundedness of the empirical image, finite entropy integral, path continuity and positive/negative supremum integrability. - AKR probabilistic knowing-how checker (2026)
    - title: AKR: A Model Checker for an Adaptative Probabilistic Knowing-How Logic
    - what: Presents AKR, an open-source Python checker for adaptive probabilistic knowing-how logic. It parses PRISM probabilistic LTS models, regular-expression perceptions, and Khq properties; builds live DFAs, synchronizes products, and delegates minimum reachability probabilities to PRISM. The paper states the polynomial recursive checking algorithm: Boolean cases recurse over states, while Khq builds a product for each perception DFA with a fresh source state and checks minimum probability of reaching DFA-final goal states. It explains NFA determinization and live-DFA conversion, AST parsing with Lark, a distinct synchronization from PRISM, strategy extraction, and output statistics. The hotel-cleaning example makes adaptation concrete: action outcomes change room-cleaning counts and plans may switch based on outcomes. Experiments vary room counts 4–100 and three regular-expression perceptions, isolating star-operator and expression-length effects.

- An End-To-End Verification of Keller’s Conjecture (2026)
    - what: Lean4 formalization resolving Keller cube-tiling conjecture in positive dimensions: true through7 and false from8 onward. Closes earlier gaps between a verified geometric-to-clique reduction and external SAT solving by verifying an improved coloring/CNF encoding, semantic symmetry transformations, certificate-checked propositional symmetry breaking and cube coverage, plus reflected checking of an8-dimensional counterexample and upward extension. Replaces arithmetic-heavy graph vertices by Keller colorings with Gap/No-Faceshare predicates; this enables the general s=2^(n−1) reduction to be solved directly at n7,s64, avoiding difficult unformalized discretization reductions to s3/4/6. Splits symmetry obligations at the conditional index-bit-flip boundary: this transformation is proved semantically in Lean, remaining clauses are manually designed and mechanically checked with substitution redundancy. Uses trestle’s scoped auxiliary variables and verified encoding combinators; optimized case splitting and checked cube-cover refutation complete the automated proof chain.
    - limits: Tiling means axis-aligned translates of half-open unit cubes with exactly one covering cube for every point of R^n. Faceshare means corners differ by1 on one axis and agree on all others. This does not cover rotated cubes, overlaps, gaps or other tile shapes. The positive-dimension restriction matters: the displayed reduction theorem uses dimension n+1. The geometric reduction uses periodic tilings, finite clique/coloring existence with s=2^(n−1), and proof of encoding soundness in the direction needed to infer absence of colorings from UNSAT. Verifying only the SAT certificate would not suffice without those upstream connections. The authors avoid relying on Kisielewicz/Łysakowska discretization results, which Clune had not formalized, by solving s64 directly. Rows with s2 or s6 are additional experiments, not substitutes for the full n7 proof. Initial fixed-color symmetries for n≥3 assume the conjecture in dimension n−1. The authors prove n2 directly and proceed successively, rather than assuming the desired lower-dimensional cases. A unit-clause symmetry restriction is valid by existence of a transformed solution, not because every original solution satisfies it. Coordinate/color permutations and bit flips preserve the coloring conditions. Conditional index bit flips may change index adjacency yet preserve No-Faceshare. They are not expressible in the employed SR proof system; that portion requires separate Lean reasoning. The remaining SR clauses were found manually, not discovered automatically by a verified symmetry search. SR addition preserves satisfiability through a repair substitution and checked unit propagation, rather than necessarily preserving every satisfying assignment. Unverified C dsr-trim adds hints; verified trestle LSR checking validates its output. Failed or wrong hint generation should not be accepted merely because the converter terminates. The stated single-threaded CaDiCaL solving and proofix split suggestions are heuristic/unverified producers; solver results have certificates checked by verified LRAT/SR tools, and the cube-cover condition is separately refuted with negated cubes. The paper reports proof by reflection into Lean; it does not give a complete axiom/native-evaluation/trusted-executable inventory in this proceedings description. CNF auxiliaries yi,j,d and zi,j,d impose the implications needed for encoding, not an unconditional biconditional identification in every model. Exactly-one color constraints are essential for deriving color inequality from the no-shared-color clauses. Reported solve/check totals are hours over all cubes; they are not specified as elapsed wall time or normalized by a stated hardware/thread configuration. No CPU, RAM, repetitions or variance is supplied. Qualitative comparisons to BHMN are not a controlled ablation isolating encoding, splits and tooling. Authors explicitly report no LLM/AI use for the formalization; paper-writing use was limited to occasional Tikz-style questions. Thus this is evidence for human-designed hybrid formal proof workflows, not a measured LLM proof-agent success.

- APR safety/liveness framework (2026)
    - title: Abstract Framework for All-Path Reachability Analysis toward Safety and Liveness Verification (Full Version)
    - what: Reformulates all-path reachability (APR) proof rules for abstract reduction systems so they correspond one-to-one with LCTRS rules, adapts cyclic APR proofs, reduces safety properties to partial APR validity, and introduces total validity that quantifies over finite and infinite execution paths for liveness. Defines DVP+ and a complete disproof rule DVP-bottom, proves equivalence with the original DVP, and formalizes finite APR pre-proofs, bud/companion links and proof graphs. Safety APR predicates characterize non-reachability of error states, illustrated with Peterson mutual exclusion. For liveness, Theorem 6.3 proves that an APR proof graph is acyclic iff the APR predicate is totally valid; the Peterson starvation-freedom example obtains an acyclic proof. Appendices establish decidability under finite reachable closure and detail limitations of reduction and cyclic generalization.
    - number: DVP and DVP+ define the same partially valid predicates
    - number: partial validity considers finite maximal paths; total validity considers finite and infinite paths
    - number: Theorem 6.3: acyclic proof graph iff total validity for a partially valid APR proof
    - number: APR proof/disproof decidability when reachable closure finite and side conditions decidable
    - limits: ARS reductions may be nondeterministic; partial validity alone ignores infinite paths and is insufficient for liveness. Total-validity criterion assumes a partially valid APR proof and its finite proof graph; decidability additionally needs finite reachable closure and decidable emptiness/intersection/runnability. Current cyclic buds must match companions exactly, the full cut rule is omitted, and process fairness/generalized companions are future work. Safety reduction uses error sets and normal-form conditions.

Trigger events are treated as available; synchronization/event availability and compatibility of component contracts need separate system-level proofs. Exactly one simple leaf node is active; composite states with multiple active nodes are excluded. Invariant I is supplied manually as a design/environment assumption. Initial satisfaction and preservation by other components are environmental obligations. Checking a component under I does not establish that the deployed sensor/memory/environment enforces I or that interacting components are mutually consistent. The CSP notion permits successful termination through Skip. It is the deadlock_freeSKIPS variant,not the usual never-terminating deadlock-free CSP process. Coinductive DFI requires a nonempty observable event sequence before recursion,while DFI* permits empty sequences after progress is already accounted for. Correctly distinguishing those variants prevents unguarded circular proof. Isabelle/HOL and the HOL-CSP semantic libraries support kernel-checked proofs of generated logical terms. Model translation runs through Eclipse EOL RoboChart→Circus and EGL Circus→HOL-CSP; the paper claims semantic faithfulness but does not give a machine-checked end-to-end translator correctness theorem. Enrichment adds an explicit active-node parameter,final-state branch and assume/guar wrappers. Equivalence to the original process is conditional on successful contracts and surrounding operational structure. Assuming an invariant is a meaningful restriction on admissible inputs,not an unconditional theorem about the original unrestricted model. False assume emits aviol and recurses to a fallback; false guar emits gviol then STOP. These behaviors differ. Component proofs distinguish environmental violations from internal errors; a deadlock-free enriched process can still rely on an unrealized environment contract. Automation is specialized to the prototypical Trans structure and available normalization/reduction rules. Simple logical/arithmetic goals use simp,auto or Sledgehammer. A failed tactic does not establish a deadlock; Nitpick/Quickcheck witnesses of uncovered guards must be assessed for reachability,environment assumptions and the actual original model. Counterexample search concentrates on enabled-guard coverage. It does not claim completeness for arbitrary transition action failure,interacting process deadlock or infinite-state reachability. - B3 VC generator formalization (2026)
    - title: Formalization of a Realistic Verification-Condition Generator for an Intermediate Verification Language
    - what: Reports Dafny definitions and soundness proofs for a B3 intermediate verification language, an executable verification-condition generator (VCG), and a coinductive reference semantics supporting nondeterminism, unbounded loops, scopes, abrupt exits and recursive calls. Proves valid generated conditions imply procedure correctness for a closed set of procedures. A structural invariant/specification semantics makes most proofs amenable to SMT automation; a separate coinductive refinement connects it to reference execution. The authors report Cursor auto-completion only, without an LLM evaluation. Postcondition stacks model escape depth while continuation stacks guide VCG control flow and variable removal. Fresh variable incarnations distinguish assignment histories from current program states. The general statement theorem connects an arbitrary symbolic context, incarnation map and continuation stack to a reconstructed scoped statement; procedure soundness is derived from an assume-pre/body/check-post wrapper. Mutual coinduction handles both recursive procedure calls and loop unrolling. The paper explicitly separates the verified formal generator from incremental SMT interaction and evolved public B3, and excludes user axiom definitions.
    - number: No runtime or benchmark evaluation is reported in the extracted text. The only quantitative proof-engineering datum is that coinductive proofs required about 100 lines of manually supplied Dafny proofs outside existing automation.
    - limits: Only source-IVL-to-VC generation is proved sound. Source-to-B3 translation, B3-expression-to-SMT translation and actual solver validity remain outside the theorem. The conclusion is conditional on mathematical validity of every generated VC, not on any unchecked SMT response. Dafny, its own verification pipeline, logic and underlying SMT automation are trusted for the author-reported proofs; no independently checked small-kernel certificate or self-verifier proof is supplied here. The paper simplifies the grammar: Boolean/integer/uninterpreted types; mathematical operations, quantified expressions and function calls; check/assume, assignment, nondeterministic choice, conditionals, unbounded loop, vars scopes and escape depths. It assumes unique variable declarations with no shadowing. Only distinct-variable inout parameters are shown; the accompanying formal implementation handles all parameter kinds, as does B3. Interpreted-function semantics and expression refinements are described but omitted from printed formal definitions. Correctness is partial: nontermination is permitted, and the work does not prove termination of B3 loops or recursive source procedures. VCG itself is reported terminating by measures on statements and continuations. Assertions must hold on relevant execution prefixes; reference omnisemantics is not merely an arbitrary overapproximation that can hide a failing check, since Check demands both the expression and post-state membership. Omnisemantics relates a statement and initial state to a sequence of overapproximating post-state sets. Its head handles normal completion; index i handles escape i. A scope duplicates the current head, adds arbitrarily initialized fresh locals, and lifts every post-set by allowing those locals and projecting them away. An escape does not execute the rest of its current statement sequence: it targets the indexed enclosing-scope postcondition. Escape zero is a no-op. A loop introduces no control-flow scope. To break out, wrap it in vars and use escape 1. Structural loop semantics existentially chooses any suitable invariant state set containing the initial state and preserved by normal body completion; body escapes still answer to the unchanged tail of enclosing postconditions. The syntactic invariant annotation is ignored by the semantics and is separately validated by VCG. Reference loop semantics instead unrolls body;loop using a greatest fixed point. Structural call semantics checks the instantiated precondition and universally considers post-states satisfying the instantiated postcondition, with the same domain and all nonargument variables unchanged. It omits checking the callee body. Reference call semantics adds RefMeetsSpec for the callee. A procedure without a body is treated as meeting its specification; its specification remains an assumption, not a proved implementation. Aliased inout actuals are excluded by the displayed distinct-variable requirement. Theorem 1 requires a closed set of procedures: every called procedure belongs to that set. Valid VCs for every procedure imply all reference MeetsSpec predicates. Recursive specifications may be assumed modularly only because all available bodies are checked and the mutually recursive reference predicates are coinductive. The article does not present a global liveness theorem or a termination argument for arbitrary recursion. Proof decomposition: Lemma 2 derives structural MeetsSpec from one procedure’s valid VCs; Lemma 3 derives reference MeetsSpec for a closed, structurally correct procedure set. Theorem 4 is the generalized statement-level VCG invariant used for Lemma 2. Several prose cross-references call Lemmas 2/3 Theorems 2/3; the numbered statement labels remain Lemma 2 and Lemma 3. VCG state contains incarnation map I, symbolic path context C and stack B of (introduced variables, continuation statements). Check generates C implies substituted E and leaves C unchanged; assume conjoins substituted E. Assignment creates a globally fresh incarnation xprime, constrains it to E evaluated under the old map, then updates I. This freshness and substitution bookkeeping is part of soundness, not a source-level assignment simplification. Conditional generation follows each branch with its continuation under opposite guard assumptions and unions the VC sets. Scope entry allocates local incarnations and pushes its following statement with its local-variable set. Normal and abrupt scope exit remove local entries from I, while accumulated formulas may still mention their incarnation values. The paper describes this symbolic-execution choice as more stable for automation but potentially producing more VCs; it gives no comparative measurement. Theorem 4 assumes all free variables in S and B are mapped by I; each jump depth fits its corresponding continuation suffix; the stated VCG judgment holds; every VC is valid; and incarnation state ist satisfies C. It concludes structural correctness of mkScope(S,B) from AdjustState(ist,I) against the universal post-set. AdjustState projects current program values from I-selected incarnations; conflating it with the full symbolic-history state would misstate the theorem. Printed equation (2) gives mkScope(S,B)=mkScope(Bprime,(vars nu in S);Sprime) in the nonempty case, reversing the declared statement/continuation argument order. Reader diagnosis: the type-consistent intended recurrence is mkScope((vars nu in S);Sprime,Bprime). This is a presentation issue; no claim is made that the Dafny implementation contains the same error. The detailed inductive proof of Theorem 4 is delegated to the artifact. Coinductive SemRefine and MeetsSpecRefine are mutually recursive greatest lemmas. Structural loop-unrolling first proves Sem(body;loop,...); the coinductive hypothesis gives RefSem of that unrolling. Calls invoke the procedure refinement, which in turn invokes statement refinement for all precondition states. Recursive interpreted expressions require a similar omitted refinement. About 100 manually supplied proof lines connect the semantics; this is not the size of the full soundness proof. The formal AST/state, semantics, generator and proofs total about 4.7 kLoC: about 2.0 kLoC AST/state, 660 LoC omnisemantics, and about 2.0 kLoC VCG/proofs. Roughly 1.5 kLoC are actual code and 3 kLoC annotations/proofs. Authors report four months by one person previously inexperienced with Dafny proofs. These are rounded development-effort reports without timing trials, benchmark corpus, proof acceptance rates or independent reproduction. Manual proof work concentrated in incarnation/substitution chains, sequence folds for continuation unwinding, and quantified/uninterpreted expression semantics. The paper calls these higher-order semantics difficult for SMT. It does not measure how much automation replaced manual work or compare alternative provers. The GenAI declaration says only Cursor auto-completion was used; it gives no model, prompts, accepted-completion counts or agent autonomy evidence. The formalized VCG stays close to the public B3 generator but is not a verified release of every public-tool path. Public B3 sends branch contexts incrementally to SMT and has evolved; integrating proofs into a release remains future work. User-defined axiom definitions are excluded; public lazy delivery of axioms and interpreted-function definitions is also future work. Thus the abstract phrase realistic features does not mean all current B3 features are covered. Artifact is linked at https://github.com/dafny-lang/b3, Software Heritage swh:1:dir:1795668a148637332f93759bb96a4cd4283d6e32, DOI 10.4230/artifacts.27039. No artifact files, source-build logs, generated binary or model of the compiler/runtime were inspected. Related claims about HOL4/Dafny, core Why3, Viper, Boogie certification and Featherweight VeriFast are author comparisons, not independent re-evaluations in this reading.

    - title: CaMeLoT: CaMeL orchestrated with Temporal logic for static verification and liveness
    - what: CaMeLoT extends the CaMeL agent-defense framework with pre-execution verification of generated plans. It translates restricted Python plans into finite-state transition systems labeled with tool calls, provenance, taint, and history predicates, checks CTL security and task properties with nuXmv, and returns counterexamples for plan repair. - CTL* on Infinite Families (2026)
    - title: CTL* Model Checking on Infinite Families of Finite-State Labeled Transition Systems
    - what: Develops compositional CTL* model checking for infinite families of finite-state labeled transition systems represented by hyperedge replacement grammars (HRGs). A Büchi-automaton-based M-equivalence and M-behaviour abstraction recolors grammar nodes while preserving family structure. The method decomposes a generated graph as context J, production rule R, and component graphs K, then summarizes exposed-node traces with finite M-behaviours. Theorem 2 proves M-equivalence is an HGV congruence; Theorem 3 proves sound and complete recoloring. LTL recoloring uses bottom-up and top-down fixed points, and CTL* recursively recolors subformulae; HRG minimization controls growth.     - title: Merge-width and First-Order Model Checking
    - what: Introduces radius-r merge-width via construction sequences that merge vertex parts and resolve default edges/nonedges. It unifies structural graph parameters and proves first-order model checking is fixed-parameter tractable on classes of bounded merge-width when a witnessing construction sequence is supplied. The paper defines construction/merge sequences, radius-r width, and translations from twin-width, degeneracy, bounded expansion, clique-width, generalized coloring numbers, and flip-width. It proves bounded twin-width and bounded expansion imply bounded merge-width, bounded merge-width implies bounded flip-width, and gives almost-bounded results for nowhere-dense classes. The model-checking algorithm maintains local first-order types through merge and resolve operations; distance-FO locality and scatter types yield Theorem 5.4, with O_{σ,q,w}(|V|²m) for a sequence of length m and O_{q,w}(|V|³) for graphs. Closure under first-order interpretations/transductions is proved. Examples and case arguments include bounded-degree/degenerate graphs, planar/minor-excluding classes, ordered structures, graph squares, and the relationship to twin-width and clique-width.

- Enhancing Interactive Theorem Prover Error Messages with Hints (2026)
    - what: Heuristic enhancements to three Agda v2.8.0 error messages, evaluated with novice-Agda programmers in a university course. Measures successful repairs, time among retained successful submissions and perceived helpfulness. Confusable hints improve measured success and speed; correct whitespace hints improve retained-success timing; correct hints consistently improve perception. Incorrect hints show no statistically significant performance effect in this study, which is not an equivalence or harmlessness theorem. Documents exactly when each hint is shown, false-positive/false-negative limits, counterbalanced error-message variants on distinct snippets, timing-data exclusions and uneven participation. Results separate objective repair outcomes from subjective ratings. Conditional timing, repeated observations per participant and unsupported no-practical-danger language materially limit generalization to proof-development or agent workflows.

Recruitment during lecture limits population to that course and language/demographic setting. Two survey variants swap original/enhanced error messages (OEM/EEM) across distinct A/B or C/D tasks. Every participant may see both conditions across different snippets, without seeing the same snippet twice. Per-snippet comparisons are between participants; pooled observations reuse participants. This is not a simple all-hints versus no-hints participant split. Ten one-error snippets represent three correct hint types and two incorrect ones, with two snippets per type/intention. No incorrect Confusable task was included because authors found no sufficiently realistic scenario. Incorrect hints are therefore a selected set, not all possible harmful hints. Whitespace heuristic splits an unknown name into in-scope names, without proving resulting application typechecks. Confusable compares unknown names only against in-scope names using generic Unicode spoof data. TooFewArgs triggers at function application sites with inferred function result type, not bare references with zero supplied arguments. Heuristics do not rerun a repair and certify its correctness. Compiler stops at the first error, making interpretation of a subsequent failure ambiguous. No semantic-correctness proof of suggested edits or trust theorem for modified Agda is presented. After removing 17 single-open/no-rating participants, analysis has 56 participants (32/24 variants), 412 submissions (228/184), average about 7 tasks and median 10; task response count 37–55. Random task ordering activated only after first TooFewArgs#A, so all users saw that task first. Timing analysis removes 136 failures, nine successful submissions interleaved with other tasks and 25 with >2-minute compilation gaps. Thus 242 retained successful observations inform timing, not all attempts. Successful-case conditioning and missingness can change group composition; results do not measure time-to-success including failures. Single-tailed Mann–Whitney U tests use directional hypotheses chosen by correct/incorrect intention, p<0.05. Table 3 has 21 p-values across five type/intention groups plus two pooled summaries and three outcomes. No multiplicity correction or participant-cluster model is described; pooled independence and multiple testing are reader concerns, not rerun statistical results. Online environment uses Haskell highlighting, no Agda Unicode-entry support or cursor-column display, and snippets use visible small libraries rather than standard Agda library. This differs from normal local Agda editing. Eleven-day access and 1–2-minute advice do not impose a strict per-task time limit. Subjective ratings range very misleading through very helpful, plus did-not-read option; Table 3 labels epsilon no rating. Exclusion of disengaged participants and differing availability of ratings affect denominators. No long-term learning/retention, error fatigue or realistic multi-error proof-development study is performed. Non-significant incorrect-hint performance tests do not establish zero harm or an acceptable bounded harm. No equivalence margin, confidence interval or statistical-power calculation is reported. The authors recommendation is broader than the exact study sample evidence. Only stated GenAI use is activated GitHub Copilot in PyCharm during data analysis. Hints themselves are designed heuristics, not evaluated LLM-generated hints or proof attempts. No Verus, verified Rust, TLA+ or distributed protocol result is supplied.     - what: Reports Isabelle/HOL verification of termination, soundness and completeness for Descartes-based real root isolation: classical interval bisection Dsc and a Newton-accelerated NewDsc. Uses existing sign-variation and Three Circles theorems, proves a Bernstein splitting lemma to justify discarding gaps, and refines to fraction-free integer-coefficient SML code. Eight small benchmark cases compare with a customized verified Sturm baseline. The authors report mixed results using ChatGPT 5.1 Thinking for newdsc proofs; they also used ChatGPT to help write the SML benchmark driver, without specifying its model. Partial recursive definitions expose a domain predicate, separating termination assumptions from conditional correctness. Square-free complex-root separation plus Three Circles proves bisection terminates. NewDsc accepts a much smaller window only if it preserves the interval’s variation count; a strengthened splitting lemma excludes roots in discarded gaps and on window boundaries. A list-of-lists de Casteljau triangle supports sign-combinatorics induction. Integer coefficient pre-scaling eliminates rational GCD overhead before SML generation. General integer input needs a square-free factorization and a global Cauchy root bound, which are future wrapper work rather than a completed all-roots interface here. Descartes counts positive roots with multiplicity and bounds them by coefficient sign variations after removing zeros; the difference is even. The displayed dsc_sound assumes domain membership, degree bound, P≠0 and a<b. The displayed dsc_complete assumes domain membership, degree bound and P≠0 and says every root strictly between a,b lies between the endpoints of some output pair. Otherwise try windows of the same scale around endpoint corrections lambda=a−nu P(a)/Pprime(a), then from b. If both jumps fail, bisect, test the exact midpoint and recurse on both halves with Nprime=max(4,floor(sqrt(N))). This does not by itself exclude roots at u or v; the paper explicitly invokes a strengthened lemma for these boundary cases but does not display that stronger formula. Treat boundary exclusion as a reported formal lemma, not a consequence of the weaker printed inequality alone. The de Casteljau triangle takes convex combinations with positive weights summing to one. Its two boundaries encode the subinterval Bernstein coefficients. Inserting a convex combination between adjacent real numbers cannot add sign changes. This differs from the cited Rocq pointwise-recursive algebraic representation because the current proof needs coefficient-list combinatorics. Nonempty tokens justify first-character access. §3.3: R-Path means the relation holds at each adjacent pair. Slicing preserves it. Concatenating nonempty paths needs one boundary relation check; empty sequences need their ordinary boundary-free cases. The displayed indexing equivalence omits that qualification. A constant number of relation checks is not constant character work: prefixMatch traverses the first token plus one character and considers rule languages, with rule/token/cache costs. §3.5: disjoint-character separator tokens provide a sufficient special case.     - title: Constraint-Driven Modeling Enabling Dual Model Checking and Simulation for Discrete Event Systems
    - what: Introduces Constraint-DEVS, a bounded variant of Parallel DEVS, and extends DEVS-Suite so the same component models support simulation and exhaustive reachability/model checking. A state-exploration protocol wraps one-cycle simulation, with bounded state variables, bounded ports, discrete-time events, selective state exploration, and transducer-based trace/property analysis. NoC and circular-buffer models demonstrate the framework. The paper gives concrete finiteness conditions and an algorithm: state and port values are specified by regular expressions, input events include an explicit null value, and a Q/V/U exploration loop injects every possible input into each reachable state, using simulation for one cycle. It defines explorable versus unexplorable variables to reduce state space without changing simulation behavior, and reuses an experimental-frame generator/transducer for state, path, and QoS-like checks. The circular buffer verification catches a simultaneous-event bug; NoC experiments compare round-robin and adaptive task distribution and quantify the severe state-explosion tradeoff. An appendix details VerifiableAtomic, StateVar/PortState, VerificationEngine, and integration with existing simulator classes.

Selective state exploration can omit information needed by a property, and complex Java data/trace processing raises cost. Results are reachability checks, not automatic proof of an unbounded DEVS model. NoC models simplify packet/data behavior and rely on abstraction; the framework does not remove state explosion: a 4x4 network was not completed, and authors propose partial verification and multiresolution modeling.     - what: Yolo separates a fast unverified heap-entailment simplifier from later Lean proof reconstruction. Mixed native-expression/list syntax and extensible operator tags retain host-language terms and permit operator-specific simplification and proofs. Integrates with Iris-Lean and relational LGTM; evaluates interactive and reconstructed runtimes against several separation-logic automation systems. Details how CFML-style six-component symbolic simplification becomes list manipulation with a recorded tacticScript, followed by replay of list-based soundness lemmas. Extensible plain-tag trees avoid positivity restrictions of recursively parameterized functor encodings. No full formal correctness theorem for all metaprogramming code is presented in the paper. Generic integration requires MoSeL BIBase/BI instances and the algebraic/soundness lemmas used by handlers. Adding an operator’s unverified Eval/equality/parsing instances is insufficient for foundational certification; each simplification handler needs its proof justification. The implementation only automates supported core operators and registered extensions. Unknown connectives remain unchanged. Iris-specific modalities in the example still require IPM tactics. Generic extensibility does not establish automatic proof search or completeness for arbitrary separation logics. Native Lean Expr and isDefEq retain polymorphic/dependent host terms, but definitional matching is heuristic and does not establish arbitrary semantic equivalence. The positivity-safe opT tree carries a plain operator tag and arbitrary argument list; its type alone does not enforce an operator’s arity. Checked reconstruction is the relevant boundary. Table1 baseline is Splean’s Lean port of CFML-style xsimpl, not a direct Rocq CFML execution comparison. Synthetic competitors share only shuffled conjunction cancellation. HTT uses equality of disjoint heap unions, while other frameworks prove entailments. Different logics, host languages, tactic interfaces and measurement methods limit ranking beyond those tasks. Pulse comparison is against Yolo’s unverified phase; Bedrock/iFrame figures explicitly include reconstruction. Machine: Dell Ubuntu workstation,5.4GHz Intel i7-14700. Zenodo software link and GitHub are provided but were not inspected or executed by reader. The paper does not evaluate verified C/Rust execution, distributed protocols, TLA+, liveness, LLM agents or generated specifications. Iris is a concurrency-capable framework, but integration and entailment benchmarks do not by themselves prove a concurrent application correct.

MOPMC implements CPU/GPU policy/value iteration and exports schedulers. The TA-to-MDP conversion separates mutually exclusive branching guards (probabilistic underdetermination) from equivalent-guard choice states (design nondeterminism), estimates guard probabilities from distributions or simulation, and encodes controller cost, lane departure, TTC and headway as total rewards. The HighwayEnv case trains DDPG without delay, then injects fixed/random observation-action delays; at 0.30 s average random delay, no-switch lane departure is 0.2849. A four-configuration switch and convex query find a minimum-MSE point (ExpCTL 1.9, PRTTC .0377, PRHW .2189, ProbLD .1720), and exported schedules improve TTC/headway while increasing lateral departure risk. Perturbing transition probabilities ±1.5–15% gives stable median outputs. Runtime experiments vary switch size, objective count to 100, and the Team Formulation Protocol, showing GPU gains on large models but mixed results on small ones.

- Multi-Objective SMC with LSS (2026)
    - title: Multi-Objective Statistical Model Checking using Lightweight Strategy Sampling
    - what: Introduces the first statistical model-checking approach for multi-objective Pareto queries. It samples deterministic strategies with lightweight strategy sampling (LSS), estimates all objective values by Monte Carlo confidence intervals, and constructs convex-hull underapproximations and incremental overapproximations of the achievable/Pareto set. The paper formalizes simultaneous confidence boxes across strategies and objectives using Bonferroni/union-bound error allocation. Its incremental algorithm assigns geometrically shrinking error budgets to batches and almost surely converges, under ideal LSS on finite contracting MDPs, to a confidence band of precision sqrt(2d) epsilon. Three fixed-budget algorithms (weight-vector refinement, fixed-iteration budget, fixed-strategy budget) combine strategy-discarding heuristics with an independent evaluation phase to retain sound lower bounds. The modes implementation evaluates 40 instances from quantitative-verification and reinforcement-learning benchmarks, and reports when SMC remains usable while Storm PMC times out.

    - number: SMC solved all fixed-budget runs where PMC timed out on large RL cases; e.g. 26.1M-state deep-sea and 40.6M-state breakable-bottles instances were handled in seconds
    - number: configuration 3 (3333 initial strategies, n=30 runs, I=10) won most heuristic/algorithm comparisons
    - limits: Models are finite contracting MDPs, so runs terminate almost surely and deterministic memoryless strategies suffice; objectives are reachability probabilities or undiscounted reachability rewards. The theory assumes ideal LSS eventually samples every deterministic strategy, while implementation uses 32-bit identifiers and can miss strategies. Finite-time sampling cannot soundly overapproximate the Pareto front because an optimal strategy may never be sampled; only underapproximations have finite-time statistical guarantees.     - what: Introduces PerF, a Maude framework that composes a distributed-system model with a reusable actor-based fault injector and uses statistical model checking to predict throughput, latency and other metrics under configurable single or combined faults. The paper defines the abstraction and refinement process, extends Modest and Jani input support, and supplies a Rust prototype. Evaluation covers small stochastic automata, bounded M/M/1/100 and Weibull/Erlang queues, and file-server models compared with mcsta’s STA digital-clocks approach. The study reports how interval granularity affects accuracy, state-space size and runtime.

- Schirrmacher et al. FO+dp (2026)
    - title: Model Checking Disjoint-Paths Logic on Topological-Minor-Free Graph Classes
    - what: Proves an algorithmic meta-theorem: model checking first-order logic extended with vertex-disjoint-path predicates is fixed-parameter tractable on graph classes excluding a fixed graph as a topological minor, with runtime f(H,phi)*n^3 and a witness tuple when the formula is true. Proof strategy decomposes graphs into strongly unbreakable tree decompositions, collapses FO+dp predicates to FO on unbreakable regions containing large clique minors, computes bounded-size folio/type-preserving representatives for boundaried subgraphs, proves compositionality under gluing, and runs a bottom-up dynamic program. The collapse uses generic folio and partition-linkedness lemmas; replacement preserves topological-minor exclusion, unbreakability, and annotated types. The result improves the earlier minor-free theorem and yields O(f(k)n^3) applications such as F-Topological Minor Deletion when a large clique certifies a no-instance.

    - what: Formalizes in Lean/mathlib a chain from probability spaces for discrete-time Markov chains through optimal expected costs of MDPs and sound expectation calculi to correctness of HeyVL encodings for probabilistic programs. Covers unbounded loops,nondeterminism,resource ticks and failed observations. Adds a fault-tolerant calculus to establish liberal-preexpectation soundness with conditioning,and idle k-(co)induction that preserves values of variables unmodified by the loop. Provides a deep embedded verification-condition generator and a small interactive proof case. This is foundational encoding/logic verification,not end-to-end verification of the production Caesar implementation or a new distributed-protocol case study. Theorem3 constructs a probability measure over infinite valid paths with cylinder probabilities equal to finite transition products; reconciles textbook path cylinders with mathlib measure cylinders via successor-of-finite-path spaces,Ionescu-Tulcea and pushforward. History-dependent deterministic schedulers induce Markov chains whose states are paths. Expected nonnegative extended-real cost is a supremum of finite-horizon path sums. Theorem12 gives angelic/maximizing Bellman least-fixed-point equality generally; Theorem19 gives demonic/minimizing equality for finitely branching MDPs by constructing an optimal memoryless scheduler,avoiding an unjustified interchange of infimum and supremum. pGCL has dependent typed states and shallow function-valued expressions inside a deep program syntax; small-step rules lead to a sink-extended operational MDP. The soundness recipe sandwiches an expectation transformer against a higher-order Bellman least fixed point. wp includes tick costs and a least loop fixed point; wlp uses one-bounded expectations,a greatest loop fixed point and ignores ticks. wfp uses least loop fixed points and counts failed observations; complementing expectations and swapping the nondeterminism optimization relates it to wlp. Conditional expectation is defined as wp/wlp(1),rather than a compositional transformer. Idle induction checks states agreeing with the initial values of all unmodified variables. HeyLo is deeply embedded with Nat,ENNReal,Bool variable types; HeyVL is loop-free and its computable vp produces formulas. Syntax-level spGCL loops carry invariants. - Spatiotemporal robustness for STL (2026)
    - title: Spatiotemporal Robustness of Temporal Logic Tasks Using Multi-Objective Reasoning
    - what: Defines spatiotemporal robustness (STR) for discrete-time temporal-logic tasks as the Pareto-maximal set of jointly admissible spatial and temporal perturbation magnitudes. It gives sound under-approximating robust semantics with min/max operations over Pareto sets, predicate-level algorithms and case studies for fighter-jet and robotaxi trajectories. STR treats spatial noise and asynchronous per-signal time shifts as separate objectives; a scalar pair of independent robustness values can be unsound. For STL in positive-normal form, robust semantics recursively combine predicate STR using downward-closure min/max. Theorem 1 proves every robust-semantic point is dominated by a true STR point, yielding sound task satisfaction but conservative margins. Predicate STR is reformulated as a monotone worst-case-margin constraint; Algorithm 1 scans temporal shells and solves robust spatial optimization, with a signed-distance shortcut from 1-Lipschitzness. Algorithm 2 propagates Pareto envelopes through parse trees.

- Structural Liveness of Conservative Petri Nets (2026)
    - what: Proves EXPSPACE-completeness of structural liveness for conservative and structurally bounded Petri nets, with doubly-exponential bounds on minimal live markings. The paper models Petri nets as action vectors and develops a proof chain: reversible virtual reachability is represented by bounded linear systems; conservative, structurally bounded and live-bottom-SCC properties are related; dead markings are represented by disjunctions of bounded restricted markings; quasi-dead markings and extractor cases reduce non-liveness to linear-system constraints. Small-solution theorems then yield a 2-exp bound on a live marking, enabling an exponential-space nondeterministic algorithm. A strengthened EXPSPACE lower bound completes hardness for conservative nets and transfers it to structurally bounded nets. The proof extends integer-solution bounds with divisibility constraints.

- The Rocq-NN-Roll Prover: Soundly Verifying Hyperproperties of Neural Networks in Rocq (2026)
    - what: Reports a Rocq implementation and soundness/completeness proof for checking rational piecewise-affine feed-forward neural networks against finite-arity universal relational specifications. Reduces a network plus hyperproperty to a joint piecewise-affine function, enumerates affine segments and searches each segment for a negative satisfaction value by a verified mixed-strictness Fourier–Motzkin solver. Provides monotonicity/robustness examples and a small nine-network runtime experiment. Printed solver theorem and robustness example contain concrete inconsistencies, which this record separates from uninspected artifact correctness. A computational real-subset interface and reduced-rational dependent type support evaluation while retaining embeddings into reals. Total piecewise-affine functions prevent partial-domain gaps from vacuously proving network properties. The formal specification restricts input preconditions to a convex polyhedron and both generator/satisfaction maps to total piecewise-affine functions. A specification-equivalence proof guards manual encoding, then verified decomposition, segment splitting and strict-negative feasibility compose into the final boolean iff theorem. Prototype limits and differing GitHub/evaluated-artifact content are explicit.
    - limits: Targets feed-forward, finite piecewise-affine networks with rational arithmetic, exemplified by affine Linear and elementwise ReLU layers. It does not support arbitrary sigmoid/nonlinear activations, recurrent cycles, training correctness or deployed floating-point/parallel semantics. The formal interface generalizes to ordered real subsets with suitable operations; its computable exact solver requires division. Exact mathematical soundness does not remove a mismatch with finite-precision inference. RealSubsetOAM packages an embedding into real numbers preserving order, addition and multiplication; Coquelicot algebra/matrix support is extended around it. QDEP is the dependent subtype of rationals fixed by rational reduction, removing multiple representatives. The authors explicitly assume proof irrelevance to identify equal reduced-rational values under standard Rocq equality. Rationals with division support FME; merely being an integer subset is not enough for the solver’s division interface. AffineSegment pairs a convex polyhedron with an affine map. Segments can be partial and domain membership is tested. Total piecewise-affine functions (TPWAFs) have composition/concatenation preserving totality. Neural-network affine decomposition returns a total function. Segments can overlap at activation boundaries; a function representation must agree there, not count each segment as a distinct execution. The supported hyperproperties quantify universally over finitely many executions of the same deterministic network. Arity r is fixed in the specification. This is a finite-input/output relational class, not arbitrary temporal hyperlogic, probabilistic fairness or infinite-trace properties. The paper uses monotonicity, robustness and individual fairness as examples of this class; only monotonicity and one-dimensional robustness receive worked formal encodings. Informal NNDH uses input tuples X generated from W by netIn and output acceptance netSat>=0. Formal NNHyperproperty narrows W to a convex polyhedron, netIn to a total piecewise-affine generator and netSat to a scalar total piecewise-affine map over the restricted real subset. Thus not every mathematical relation or arbitrary precondition is accepted. - Transitive Relation Learning (TRL) (2026)
    - title: Infinite State Model Checking by Learning Transitive Relations
    - what: Presents Transitive Relation Learning (TRL), which learns transitive relational summaries while bounded-model-checking an infinite-state transition system, reducing its effective diameter until finite-depth unsatisfiability proves safety. TRL detects loops in SMT models, computes conjunctive variable projections and transitive projections from recurrence analysis, adds learned relations while forbidding consecutive use of a learned relation, and uses blocking clauses to prefer learned transitions over loops. Learned relations over-approximate for safety, so safety is sound but unknown may result; an acceleration-based under-approximation replacement reconstructs traces to prove unsafety. The implementation supports LIA relational formulas/CHCs and integrates Yices/Z3 in LoAT. The paper proves Theorem 22 (safe result implies safety) and correctness of linear-integer transitive projection, and details limitations, related interpolation/acceleration approaches, and a 626-problem CHC evaluation.

Z3 GSpacer solved 373; LoAT ABMC solved 272. TRL was strongest overall and competitive in runtime, while GSpacer led safe instances and ABMC led unsafe instances.
    - limits: The theory assumes a complete first-order theory with effective quantifier elimination; implementation is restricted to linear integer arithmetic. TRL may diverge because learned-relations generation/trace search is not guaranteed to terminate, and learned over-approximations cannot prove unsafety without acceleration. BMC unrolling can bottleneck large systems, although backtracking on loops mitigates this. Future work targets reals, bitvectors, arrays and temporal verification.

    - what: Studies a systematic bottom-up method for compositional CBMC unit proofs. - VerCors data-parallel scalability (2026)
    - title: Scalable Deductive Verification of Data-Level Parallel Programs
    - what: Improves VerCors scalability for array/matrix data-parallel programs with three linked techniques: rewrite nested quantified array expressions into equivalent single-variable forms with usable SMT triggers, use unique type qualifiers to rule out array aliasing, and use immutable qualifiers to model unchanged arrays as mathematical sequences. Kernel-body extraction further reduces solver context. Section 2 explains permission-based separation logic, Viper translation and nested GPU parallel blocks through OpenCL XswapFast and PVL examples. Section 3 defines a bijective inverse for linear index expressions, states conditions for correctness, and reports a 2,500-line Lean 4 proof of the rewrite theorem; nonlinearity and unsupported modulo patterns remain limits. Section 4 explains Viper quantified heap chunks and snapshot comparisons, then defines immutable and unique typing, including struct/pointer examples. Section 5 evaluates CLBlast BLAS kernels, earlier Halide/HaliVer benchmarks and a Radio Telescope Pipeline containing the Padre algorithm. On an i7-11800H/32GB Ubuntu 23.04 machine, ten runs per experiment and one-hour timeout show all techniques up to 150× speedup, 8.5× total Level-1 and 10.8× Level-2 CLBlast speedups, more than 1.9× on earlier experiments, and previously unverifiable xger/xher2 and Padre cases becoming verifiable. The rewriter was essential for every reported experiment; gemm_3 failed because modulo is unsupported.

    - what: Develops a statistical theory for finite-budget agentic theorem proving. It models verifier-backed proof search as a deterministic finite-horizon reachability MDP and defines statistical provability as the probability that a specified prover reaches a verified proof within a verifier-call budget on a problem distribution. Under a faithful state abstraction, optimal MDP success equals budgeted syntactic provability. For offline depth-wise action-value regression followed by greedy proving, Theorem3.1 bounds the gap to the optimal prover by an occupancy-weighted sum of value-estimation errors; the multiplier is the learned prover’s average truncated proof length. Error terms separate approximation, training-region coverage geometry and Monte Carlo rollout noise, with a faster rate under an action-gap margin condition. Defines full proof states as multisets of open goals so branching remains Markov, deterministic verifier transition F, solved set G, hitting time TG, budgeted value V and average truncated length Len. Assumption3.1 requires compact concentration sets, Lipschitz optimal values and hypothesis classes, local-mass coverage of i.i.d. query pairs, conditionally independent binary rollout labels with mean Q*, and minimax regression. Theorem3.1 gives εt=approximation+covering term+Hoeffding rollout noise and regret 2Σ unsolved-mass×ε. A margin condition changes ε to ε^(β+1). Budget allocation balances Nt and mt under total labels nt=Ntmt. Appendices prove deterministic MDP, faithful abstraction, Bellman recursion, greedy regret, covering and uniform regression; truncation adds overflow penalty δW. Appendix C proposes representation selection by Bellman-certificate tightness and a complexity penalty; Appendix D interprets scaling through horizon, effective dimension and margins.
    - number: Main bound: best success probability minus learned prover's is at most 2 times (worst per-step value error) times the learned prover's average number of checker calls before success or budget end
    - number: Under an action-gap margin condition the dependence on error improves to a fast rate
    - limits: Faithful abstraction assumes e(FR(r,a))=F(e(r),a) and exact preservation of solved states. The equality between optimal MDP success and syntactic provability follows this assumption; arbitrary learned embeddings need not be faithful. The theory is trace-local. Compact concentration Ct must cover both training queries and learned-prover comparisons, and the candidate region must retain at least one globally optimal action. The paper explicitly says a new prover leaving the occupied region is no longer certified without added coverage assumptions. Binary rollout labels are idealized verifier-backed success labels with conditional mean Q*. The paper says practical-target bias can be absorbed into ε, but the stated theorem assumes exact Q* labels and its approximation term is relative to Q*. Biased targets require an explicit allowance; reader derivation using the supplied minimax proof adds2bt when label means differ uniformly by≤bt. Repeating suboptimal-policy rollouts reduces sampling noise, not this bias. No empirical calibration is supplied. The exact minimax regression optimizer is an idealization. Numerical optimization error ξt can be added, but no practical learner, neural architecture or training algorithm is evaluated. The verifier transition is deterministic, while policy decoding, retrieval and exploration may be random. The theory addresses greedy proving; beam search, backtracking, top-k and decomposition need extra retention/suboptimality assumptions. The finite-horizon result does not remove undecidability, worst-case hardness or unknown proof existence. Statistical provability depends on q0, so a biased library workload can be easy while adversarial or uniform hard instances remain difficult. The effective dimension dt, coverage ct, Lipschitz constants, action-gap tails and occupancy curve are theoretical quantities. The paper proposes estimating them from traces as future work and reports no benchmark measurement. No Verus/Rust/TLA+/distributed-system experiment is supplied. Transfer to systems verification is an inference about replacing proof-state/verifier interfaces, not a measured claim.

- Zero-knowledge model checking (2026)
    - what: Introduces zero-knowledge model checking (ZKMC), proving that a secret reactive system satisfies a public temporal specification without disclosing its transition relation, via explicit-state KZG commitments or symbolic Farkas witnesses and folded sigma/range proofs. The framework certifies LTL/ω-regular model checking by ranking functions for the product with a complementary Büchi automaton. The explicit-state scheme commits to secret initial states/transitions and batch-proves that public counterexample states cannot be in the secret model; its certificate is two group elements while prover work is quadratic in state count. The symbolic scheme restricts systems to linear guarded commands, translates initiation/step/fairness obligations to linear-inequality unsatisfiability, uses Farkas dual witnesses, Pedersen matrix commitments, zkMatrix multiplication, Bulletproof range proofs and a Salem–Spencer one-shot fold. The prototype tests handshake, DHCP and round-robin protocols and reports separate enumeration/setup/prover/verifier timings, showing complementary scaling regimes.

    - number: symbolic dhcp_10000_3_10 (2^20.9 states) completes in under half an hour while explicit enumeration times out
    - number: round-robin rr_5 reaches 2^10.2 states and 38,427 obligations; symbolic verifier is OOM
    - limits: Soundness relies on binding/hiding commitments, knowledge-sound zkmm/zkeq/zkrp, Fiat–Shamir random-oracle modeling and field bounds avoiding integer wraparound; Farkas completeness can fail when only rational or out-of-bound witnesses exist. Explicit-state verification exposes quadratic state-space costs; symbolic verification requires linear guarded-command models, integer coefficients and piecewise-linear rankings.     - title: Formula size game and model checking for modal substitution calculus
    - what: Defines game-theoretic and formula-size semantics for MSC, GMSC, GGMSC and SC, then characterizes expressive power and model-checking complexity, including asynchronous variants and a universal reduction. The paper gives two co-inductive semantic games (bounded-round and global interpretation tracing) and proves their correctness, then builds formula-size games whose winning strategies characterize separation of classes of pointed Kripke models, including non-uniform finite-model strategies. It identifies asynchronous MSC/GMSC/GGMSC with corresponding modal mu-calculus and computation-logic fragments, and encodes deterministic linear-tape-bounded Turing machines over words. Detailed reductions establish PSPACE-completeness for standard MSC/GMSC/GGMSC and SC, PTIME-completeness for asynchronous variants, constant SC data complexity, SC satisfiability bounds, and a computable reduction from every recursively enumerable problem to MSC model checking when input padding is allowed.

    - title: Efficient Model Checking for the Alternating-Time µ-Calculus via Effectivity Frames
    - what: Implements full alternating-time µ-calculus (AMC) model checking over concurrent game frames (CGFs) and equivalent effectivity frames (EFs). Conversion precomputes coalition capabilities so modal checks become set lookups; the paper measures whether this amortizes conversion cost and compares against direct CGF checking and MCMAS. It defines CGF and playable EF semantics, proves the induced-frame translation preserves every AMC formula, and instantiates local/game-based coalgebraic µ-calculus algorithms in COOL. Random formulas, castle games and modulo games separate regimes: EF conversion has an upfront exponential-in-agents/moves cost, while EF evaluation benefits when many joint moves have equivalent outcomes or fixpoints repeatedly revisit modalities. The full AMC implementation supports Büchi-style formulas unavailable in MCMAS; MCMAS instead benefits from symbolic OBDD representations on succinct cases.

POR defines invisibility/independence and DFS conditions C1–C3, proving stuttering equivalence and preservation of sATL* under iR semantics. The result is decidable approximation because unrestricted ATLiR perfect-recall checking is undecidable.

- Automatically Generalizing Proofs and Statements (2025)
    - what: Lean proof-term generalization tactic that takes an existing proof and a selected constant, then returns a more abstract statement with a proof when transformation typechecks. It generalizes repeated occurrences independently, discovers related constants through type mismatches/antiunification, and abstracts composite proof fragments into hypotheses. Demonstrations include arithmetic, set cardinality, algebraic cancellation and Bézout. Six-stage description explains separate metavariables per occurrence, hypothesis abstraction from inferred types, iterative detection of dependent constants, unification to recover required equalities, metavariable-to-binder extraction, and type inference for the resulting statement. Contrasts accepted proof with useful/general/nonvacuous generalization, and shows how definitional computation or opaque proof steps obstruct extraction. Distinguishes implemented tactic from ideal future proof-discovery uses.
    - limits: Requires an existing formal Lean proof and user-selected expression/constant, optionally occurrence controls. Soundness relies on successful final proof typechecking in its Lean environment and the assumptions of referenced declarations. It is not a stand-alone axiomatic proof of the algorithm, an audit of input axioms, or a guarantee that a formal statement matches human intent. Accepted result is a provable conditional statement. This alone does not establish weakest hypotheses, nonvacuity, strict generality, novelty, usefulness or a canonical mathematical abstraction. Paper explicitly describes a true output hypothesis that forces n=2 and thus adds no genuine generality. Outputs depend on the exact proof, including how facts are encoded, not just the original theorem statement. The transformation operates on proof terms and loses tactic-script structure. Default abstracts all occurrences; coincidental equality may change output, and user can restrict occurrences. Dependent-constant search uses syntactic antiunification and a heuristic favoring fewer metavariables. No completeness, optimality, termination or runtime complexity theorem is reported. Related mismatches may remain unresolved, especially when generalized types lose definitional equality. Definitional-equality example fails when generalizing integers because divisibility no longer unfolds as the required existential. An explicit rewrite via Int.dvd_def records the connection as a proof step and permits an added divisibility-definition hypothesis. Merely unfold does not change the proof term and therefore does not provide that evidence. Computation can erase the dependency trace needed for abstraction:paper’s reduceMul example leaves 6 rather than how 2*3 produced it. Generalizing proofs cannot independently solve newly exposed mathematical subproblems. Original specialized computations may need to become hypotheses instead. Bézout output is a long collection of sufficient algebraic/size/quotient/remainder conditions from a particular proof, not a recovered canonical Euclidean-domain definition. Typeclass simplification and simultaneous generalization from two proofs are future work. Several application sections discuss an ideal algorithm or mathematical motivation rather than demonstrated execution:inductive proof discovery, intermediate-value abstraction, conjecture generation, learning from counterexamples, and interesting-question generation. No integrated LLM/automated proof-discovery evaluation is reported.

- Budde et al. sound SMC (2025)
    - title: Sound Statistical Model Checking for Probabilities and Expected Rewards
    - what: Surveys statistical methods used by SMC tools, identifies unsound confidence procedures, recommends Clopper–Pearson for probabilities and DKW for bounded rewards, and introduces theoretical bounding-set and limit-PAC methods for unbounded reachability rewards implemented in modes. The paper distinguishes fixed-k and sequential PAC settings and requires worst-case coverage over all true probabilities, exposing why CLT/Wald, Wilson/CC and Chow–Robbins procedures can be unsound. It proves the DKW confidence band yields a tighter expected-reward interval than Hoeffding, derives bounds for instantaneous, cumulative and reachability rewards, and shows a finite-state DTMC geometric path-length construction is theoretically sufficient but often unusably large. DKW-E-Lower is a new lower-bound procedure for any nonnegative finite-expectation random variable, with a limit-PAC theorem. A survey of tools shows no sound and efficient default for sequential probabilities or fixed reward estimation before their modes implementation.

- Canonical for Automated Theorem Proving in Lean (2025)
    - what: Presents Canonical, a Rust implementation of backward type-inhabitation search linked to Lean, using beta-normal eta-long terms, explicit substitutions, equational constraints, arbitrary argument refinement order and entropy-guided parallel iterative deepening. On an adapted Natural Number Game with manually selected premises, solves 62/74 statements versus Aesop 27 and Duper 45; reports 51 seconds for the 62 successes. Also solves 46 of the first 50 Lean Prelude statements under a specified inhabitant-equality criterion. Search supports higher-order premises, indexed types and induction, but the translation omits universes and quotients, and default iota pruning is incomplete. Separates source-dependent type theory, Rust search, translation obligations and returned Lean terms; records universe-erasure unsoundness admitted by the authors, iota/structure-eta incompleteness, manually chosen premises and benchmark adaptations, per-world results, exact proof-size metric, successful-proof timing denominator, Prelude success definition, and examples requiring supplied lemmas or generalized recursors. Distinguishes proposed LLM integration from measured proof search.
    - limits: §§3.1–3.2, pp.5–6: terms are beta-normal eta-long and have parameter bindings, simultaneous let declarations, a local head and arguments. Types annotate bindings. Parameters/lets may refer to each other circularly; the encoder must supply a signature valid in the target theory. A missing variable type prevents its use in proof construction; a missing let body makes it an opaque constant. Recursor and projection annotations add reduction behavior. Static arity is an input-format property, not a general property of Lean expressions. §3.2, p.6: start with a goal metavariable, choose a local head and create all its argument metavariables together. Refinement creates typing and definitional-equality constraints. Violations undo a head assignment; metavariable choice need not be backtracked because any completed term admits arbitrary refinement order. This is a structural algorithm argument, not a mechanized implementation-correctness theorem. §3.3, pp.6–7: de Bruijn indices with explicit substitutions permit partial beta reduction without knowing a metavariable’s eventual free variables. Reduction either exposes a rigid head/arguments or becomes stuck. Different rigid heads violate equality; equal heads yield subterm equations. Refinement revisits equations stuck on that metavariable and undo restores them. There is no separate dedicated unification algorithm; constraints guide the same search. §3.3.1, p.8: equality of a blocked recursor/projection and a rigid term may become true after the major argument is instantiated. Default mode treats it as violated, deliberately sacrificing completeness. Program-synthesis mode (+synth) treats it as stuck, admitting more search. A constructor cannot be chosen as the major-argument head of a recursor/projection because that would create a reducible term outside canonical form. This paper does not establish completeness for all Lean definitional equality. §§3.4–3.4.1, pp.8–9: iterative deepening DFS bounds a custom entropy product, mutates assignments in place and runs large branches with fork-join parallelism. Successive thresholds aim to double node counts. Refined metavariables contribute branching factors; unrefined ones use empirical completion estimates from bins keyed by source type ignoring explicit substitution and rigid-equation status. Estimated chance of later rigid equality mixes entropy 1 with average completion refinements; each metavariable estimate is capped at 1000, and unsuccessful refinements incur an extra penalty. Independence is an estimating assumption, not a proved property of dependent subgoals. §3.4.2, pp.9–10: prefer rigid equations for propagation and early failure, then statistically likely impossible metavariables, then high estimated entropy and later arguments whose types constrain earlier values. Meta-level choice and head-level choice serve different purposes. No general theorem of optimality, fair coverage under changing statistics, or global resource bound accompanies this heuristic. §4, pp.10–11: Rust solver communicates through Lean FFI and translated Term/Typ structures. Translation follows Lean Expr constructors, uses lets to retain beta-redexes, and replaces universe-indexed sorts by a single declaration Sort : Sort. The authors explicitly admit possible unsoundness by Girard’s paradox. This affects the search abstraction; a returned term accepted by Lean’s kernel would still have to satisfy Lean’s original universe rules. The paper supplies no mechanized translator-correctness proof or separate measured return-path/kernel-rejection experiment. Rust implementation alone is not evidence of verified Rust or Verus use. §§4–4.1, p.11: Pi structure packages function-valued terms to enforce static arity, with Pi.f/Pi.mk wrappers and eta expansion. Unfolds Set, Not, reducible definitions and typeclass instances where possible to avoid excess wrappers. Literal constants are generally opaque; only natural literals at most 5 receive constructor definitions. Quotient types and universe levels are outside the translation’s supported scope. §4.2, p.12: recursively include constant definitions down to primitives; provide recursor definitions as usable abstractions while hiding types of certain definition-only constants to reduce redundant expressions. Inductive declarations bring constructors/recursors, structures bring projections; local assumptions are included and users supply extra constants in brackets. Recursive expansion can violate abstraction and explode for real numbers. Relevance filtering and automatic premise selection over all Mathlib are outside scope. §5, pp.12–13: Natural Number Game has 79 levels across 9 worlds but 74 unique statements. Authors replace its pedagogical custom naturals/axiomatic operations with standard Nat. Premises are manually selected, mostly from reference solutions and earlier levels. Added Nat.le.intro/dest convert inequality definitions; one level needs Classical.byContradiction; an If structure lets Canonical encode implication induction predicates. Report results for this adapted benchmark, not the untouched game or an unseen randomly sampled theorem library. §5, p.13: Aesop uses default options, Duper portfolio mode, Canonical timeout 15 seconds. Natural-number simp attributes are removed until the corresponding game level, while Duper gets needed definitional equations. Hardware Mac Mini M4 Pro, 24GB RAM; Lean/Mathlib 4.16.0, Duper 0.0.23. Artifact reference 45 names CanonicalLean v4.22.0, distinct from the benchmark Lean version. §5, pp.13–14: 62/74 Canonical, 27/74 Aesop, 45/74 Duper. Authors attribute much advantage to induction support absent from the compared tactics. 51 seconds is explicitly the time to generate 62 successful proofs; it does not include all failed attempts as a benchmark-total wall-time measurement. On nine successes taking over one second, averages are 23 million attempted refinements/s, 2.1 million/s without equation violation and 1.2 million/s below threshold, branching factor 1.6, final iteration 17% of solve time. §5, p.14: proof length counts constants, free/bound variables, sorts, literals and projections, excluding lambda/let binder types. On common successes Canonical proofs average 251 times shorter than Duper and 18 times shorter than Aesop. Available constants and use of domain-specific lemmas differ. This metric does not measure human readability, checking time, bytes, or whole-benchmark proof-size performance. §5, p.14: Prelude test uses first 50 statements, not a random held-out set. Nonpropositions allow multiple generated inhabitants; success requires one definitionally equal to the library implementation. Constructor-disequality proofs supplied instead of noConfusion. 46 successes; three failures due to missing structure eta encoding, one due to iota incompleteness. Deterministic runtime call API, no shared-memory multiprocessing and deterministic sandbox initialization are assumed. Runtime API implementation, input state and memory protection remain trusted. §§2.1/2.2: Memory isolation is necessary to prevent reading external nondeterministic data; hardware or software isolation can provide it. Sandbox code cannot be writable and executable by untrusted code. Arm64 fixed-width alignment prevents executing alternate instruction decodings; x86 uses 32-byte instruction bundles, no spanning instructions, aligned direct targets and masked aligned indirect targets. Code/data must be separated. Unknown instruction encodings are rejected. Runtime can use a separate writable alias for loading code; this trusted action must not expose mutable code while the sandbox executes. §2.1: On Arm64, torn store straddling mapped/unmapped boundary may or may not partially alter mapped memory. DeCl terminates after a memory fault rather than simulating precise stores. This termination rule alone does not define a deterministic post-fault sandbox memory snapshot; runtime must respect the stated externally visible-effect boundary. Side-channel paragraph claims removal of in-sandbox timers/parallelism/atomic timing vectors; it does not provide an empirical side-channel evaluation or establish that an external observer cannot measure execution time. §3: Integer and integer SIMD subset only; floating-point instructions excluded because some permit implementation-dependent approximations. Initialize every block IN to all-undefined, analyze without reporting, union predecessor OUT sets, analyze again with reporting. Indirect jumps are preceded by AND alignment which defines observable flags, so static-branch CFG suffices; AF remains undefined but accepted instructions cannot observe it. A full fixpoint could accept more programs; two-pass algorithm may falsely reject but is claimed sound, and author-compiled LLVM/GCC cases pass within two. This tests handwritten verifier/ISA understanding; it is not necessary trusted enforcement, exhaustive ISA validation or proof of all accepted programs. Initial gas/counter arithmetic, runtime calls and periodic interrupt handling must satisfy implementation constraints. No arbitrary wall-clock bound follows from a gas count alone. §4.2/Figure 3: Branch scheme checks high sign bit after decrement and traps on negative. Arm SUB/TBZ/BRK preserves flags; x86 flag-preserving LEA/PUSH RCX/MOV0x3f/SHRX/JRCXZ/INT3/POP sequence is costlier than SUB/JNS/INT3 when flags may be clobbered. Indirect jumps into middle of a statically recognized block may be charged for its full length, deterministically overcharging. Forward-branch gas checks can be elided if whole program size N bounded (example10M instructions); at most N further instructions until checked backwards branch or termination. This is not exact preemption at precisely the requested instruction count. §4.3/Figure 4: Timer scheme keeps gas decrement but removes per-block sign checks; runtime checks sign before every externally visible call effect, and timer interrupt terminates negative-gas programs. Execution may continue nondeterministically after gas exhaustion for at most timer slice t, while external call trace stays deterministic. Requires calls be the only observable effects and program memory be externally invisible. Short slices add overhead; tiny gas budgets may favor branch metering. Position-oblivious code allows only low32-bit observations of absolute-address registers, zeros high bits after PC-relative address formation, and requires runtime-returned pointers be offsets too. This is stronger than ordinary position-independent executable code. §5.2: x86 CALL stores absolute return address, so POC replaces it with LEAL/PUSH/JMP; returns are aligned masked indirect branches re-adding base. String instructions must zero high32bits of RSI/RDI afterward. OR-based branch target guard flags must not reveal base: PF depends only low byte, SF requires same address-space half, ZF requires never allocating zero sandbox; LEA guard can avoid flags changes if both halves needed. Compiler/rewrite/assembler/linker are untrusted for determinism because final code is checked, but rejection or changed source-program semantics remains possible. Section8 explicitly permits replacing unwanted FP instructions with NOPs; acceptance then establishes the altered binary’s restricted behavior, not faithful implementation of original FP source. §6.2: Trusted standalone linear-time verifier decodes enumerated subset, checks instruction/configuration safety, bundle control flow, LFI addressing/reserved registers and x86 flags.     - what: Rocq/Mathematical Components verification of a functional sweep algorithm returning triangular/trapezoidal cells whose interiors and specified lateral doors avoid nonvertical segment obstacles.
