Syntax is an inductive deep embedding with bottom, variables, conjunction, implication, coalition effectivity, individual knowledge and common knowledge. Syntax itself accepts arbitrary agent types; Fintype and Nonempty hypotheses are introduced where needed. Semantics uses classical reasoning and noncomputable finite-set conversions within Lean/Mathlib. §4, p.4: effectivity E(s,G) is a family of outcome sets a coalition can force, abstracting away explicit actions and strategies. True playability requires six conditions: empty outcome never forceable, universal outcome forceable, grand-coalition maximality relative to empty-coalition complements, outcome monotonicity, superadditivity for disjoint coalitions and a least empty-coalition outcome set. These are model assumptions, not distributed runtime liveness or memory-safety claims. §4/5, pp.4–7: each individual knowledge relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive (S5-style equivalence). Coalition effectivity means the satisfying-state set belongs to E(s,G). Individual knowledge quantifies over indistinguishable states. Printed mathematical common knowledge uses a starred union relation, whereas Lean snippets use paths with at least one edge. For a nonempty coalition reflexivity bridges these conventions; empty coalition requires a different convention and exposes a discrepancy. §6/Table 1, pp.5/7: reported soundness Theorem 4 is theoremhood implies validity in the defined class of models, proved by induction on derivations. Axioms for coalition operators correspond to playability conditions; knowledge axioms use equivalence relations. Common-knowledge axiom C and induction rule RC use path-constructor arguments. This is not correctness of any specific program or natural-language requirement. §7, pp.8–9: Pformula gives constructors, Pformula_ax adds propositional derivability, CLformula adds effectivity and laws, Kformula individual knowledge, Cformula common knowledge with finite agent type. Typeclasses state minimum operations/laws; they are not generic inductive syntax. Generic semantics is omitted, so some proofs by induction remain tied to particular formula datatypes. §8.1, p.9: canonical coalition states are maximal consistent sets. For proper coalitions, X is effective iff some formula has its truth set inside X and its effectivity formula in the state. The grand-coalition case uses complements and absence of empty-coalition effectivity. Generic construction assumes nonempty agents and propositional bottom is not derivable. Initial canonical model has only five playability conditions and no epistemic relations. §8.2, pp.9–11: finite closure contains every subformula of every closure member, single negations, Ki CG ψ for members of common-knowledge groups and CG[G]ψ for effectivity formulas. Finiteness of agent groups enables finite expansion. Filtered states are canonical-state intersections with closure, represented by a filtered powerset and attached membership proof. There are at most 2^|cl(φ)| possible filtered states; this is a reader counting bound, not a paper runtime measurement. §8.2/8.3, pp.10–14: filtered effectivity treats grand coalition existentially and proper coalitions universally over canonical representatives. Finite models make empty-coalition principality follow from playability. Proofs use pairwise incompatibility of distinct filtered states and provability of the universal state disjunction. Set-to-Finset-to-List conversions require preserving disjointness, membership and absence of duplicates. §8.4/8.5, pp.14–15: Truth Lemma 5 equates filtered-state membership and satisfaction for formulas inside the finite closure. Common-knowledge proof inducts on positive-length paths from the front. Completeness Theorem 6 is validity implies theoremhood, using a maximal consistent extension of {¬φ} and a finite filtered countermodel. This establishes formula completeness/finite countermodels under the chosen semantics, not strong completeness for arbitrary infinite theories or a measured decision algorithm. §§1/3/9, pp.2–3/15–17: authors report all artifact proofs sorry-free, Lean 4.4.0-rc1 and Mathlib 98fe17fd, after completing an original Lean 3 proof and porting it. Paper snippets omit proof steps and even show an explicitly explained sorry. Code size about 6,000 lines: 300 CL, 700 CLK, 1,100 CLC and almost 4,000 shared. No exact build timings, proof-search benchmark, independent axiom audit or implementation replay provided in this reading. §9, pp.16–17: main engineering burden is finiteness/datatype conversion and long routine inductions. Native quantified representations and more generic semantics/inductive structures are proposed improvements, not implemented evaluations. IoT and metro systems motivate the introduction but are not verified cases. No Rust, Verus, TLA+, LLM agent or deployed distributed protocol experiment.

- Modular Verification of Intrusive List and Tree Data Structures in Separation Logic (2024)
    - what: A modular separation-logic method for intrusive data structures, where clients embed link nodes inside data objects. The representation separates node topology from attached data. Coq/Iris proofs in HeapLang reuse node-level specifications to verify cyclic/doubly linked lists, deques, and unbalanced binary-search-tree maps, including internal pointers and insertion. Shows that singly linked intrusive sequences compose into cycles, two oppositely directed cycles compose into a dcycle, and data fields framed alongside dcycles give a deque. For search trees, separates shape, key ordering and attached values; uses functional one-hole contexts and separating implication to retain the traversed tree while returning a pointer to an interior link. Locate is proved once and its contract makes insertion a modular, non-inductive client proof.
    - limits: Object programs are in unmodified Iris HeapLang, a simplified language with dynamic allocation, arrays and location arithmetic. The paper deliberately omits C fixed-width integers, byte representation and alignment. It does not verify actual Linux/Boost C/C++ code, C container_of provenance rules, a compiler, or machine execution. Hoare triples guarantee no crash under their ownership preconditions, and the stated result if execution finishes. This is partial correctness, not a proved termination/cost bound. The illustrated operations are sequential; the use of the concurrent Iris framework does not establish concurrent linearizability or thread-safe list mutation. Node APIs require ownership of supplied link cells and return detached ownership after removal. Clients allocate/deallocate enclosing objects. Data-layout predicates require separate ownership of topology and payload fields; arbitrary aliasing between those fields is not admitted. Concrete BST API uses natural-number keys and ordinary comparisons. Generic functional discussion uses a Boolean comparison p, but the printed assumptions/as-stated lemmas have apparent gaps detailed below. No balanced-tree invariant, rotations, deletion API or logarithmic complexity theorem is provided. Partial-tree reconstruction requires a valid one-hole context and a subtree whose insertion preserves the whole-tree BST invariant. A magic wand does not allow plugging an arbitrary key arrangement into the hole. Functional correctness lemmas and context generalization are part of the proof effort. Formal checking depends on Coq, Iris reasoning about HeapLang, and the declared definitions/specifications. Diaframe assists proof search and small pointer-arithmetic support is added in Setup.v. The paper supplies a Zenodo mechanization, but this reader has not replayed it or compared printed inconsistencies to source. The deque proof-size claim is less than30Coq proof lines for the deque API after underlying dcycle specifications, Iris lemmas and Diaframe support exist. It is not the size or cost of the full library or tree development. Scaling to more graph-like shared structures remains open.

- SCYTHE distributed protocol synthesis (2024)
    - title: Efficient Synthesis of Symbolic Distributed Protocols by Sketching
    - what: Introduces SCYTHE, a syntax-guided and counterexample-guided synthesizer for completing TLA+ sketches of parameterized distributed protocols. It enumerates typed expressions with cache/equivalence reduction and short-circuiting, uses TLC to check finite instances, and generalizes counterexamples into pruning constraints for safety, deadlock, liveness, and stuttering. The tool synthesizes protocols including consensus, 2PC, locks, sharded stores, and Raft reconfiguration. The paper formalizes protocol instances, fairness, sketches with pre/post holes and regular-tree grammars, and distinguishes finite-instance synthesis (Problem 1) from all-parameter-instance synthesis (Problem 2). Candidate generation uses cache-based size enumeration and semantic normal forms for Boolean/set/equality expressions; pruning constraints are disjunctions of hole interpretations. Safety constraints are optimal, while deadlock/liveness/stuttering encodings are sub-optimal but non-over-pruning; fairness and explicit implementability/environment constraints prevent vacuous solutions. TLC exhaustive checks each finite instance. In 22 benchmark rows, equivalence reduction cuts generated expressions by orders of magnitude; final TLAPS proofs establish safety for arbitrary instances in all but the two-process-only Peterson cases. Extra-checks expose finite-size overfitting: two Raft variants initially correct up to 3 nodes failed at 4+ and required larger-instance checks.
    - number: 22 benchmark configurations
    - number: up to >3 orders of magnitude expression reduction
    - number: raft-reconfig ID 121: 694,552 to 271 expressions
    - number: 4-node extra-check caught 3-node overfitting
    - limits: Synthesis guarantees only the finite instance checked by TLC unless an independent proof (TLAPS) establishes parameterized correctness; the search problem is generally undecidable. Grammar restrictions, typed symbols, opaque domains, finite-state verifier instances, fairness constraints, and manually specified implementability/environment separation shape results. Liveness pruning is sub-optimal; weak-fairness handling may under-prune. TLC calls dominate many runs, and the final all-instance verification remains a difficult/undecidable step. Benchmarks are adapted from existing specifications and may not represent arbitrary distributed protocols.

- SEEV ReLU neural barrier verification (2024)
    - title: SEEV: Synthesis with Efficient Exact Verification for ReLU Neural Barrier Functions
    - what: Introduces SEEV, a synthesis-and-verification loop for ReLU neural control barrier functions (NCBFs) on continuous nonlinear control-affine systems. It regularizes activation patterns along the barrier boundary and exactly checks correctness, hyperplane, and hinge conditions required by a nonsmooth Nagumo-style safety theorem. The model is xdot=f(x)+g(x)u with safe set C={h>=0} and inner set D={bθ>=0}. Proposition 1 requires feasible controls on every boundary activation set and D⊆C. Training combines correctness, derivative/feasibility, and a boundary activation regularizer; outer CEGIS adds verifier counterexamples. The verifier finds an initial boundary activation set by a line segment and LP, enumerates all boundary hyperplanes with neural breadth-first search, enumerates boundary hinges by LP, then applies cheap sufficient checks before nonlinear exact checks (dReal where needed). Theorem 2 gives a valid NCBF when all checks pass. Experiments on Darboux, obstacle avoidance, hi-ord8 and spacecraft rendezvous show major speedups; SR 6D L4/M8 falls from 298.7s baseline to 60.1s, while dReal/Z3 are unavailable or time out in many cases. Regularization cuts SR boundary hyperplanes from 6218 to 627 at equal coverage in one configuration.

- The Rewster: Type Preserving Rewrite Rules for the Coq Proof Assistant (2024)
    - what: Extends Coq definitional reduction with user rewrite rules and presents a bidirectional type-preservation criterion for PCUIC with universe cumulativity and SProp proof irrelevance. Pattern types and metavariable types are inferred generally; right sides are checked against those types, optionally using equality constraints safely forced by a well-typed match. Coq implementation is reported, while confluence checking and justified conservative rules remain future work. Explains why checking a propositional equality at some common type is unsound under cumulativity and why ordinary unification can infer unjustified symbol injectivity. Gives higher-order metavariable substitution, restricted symbol-headed patterns, triangle/confluence restrictions, a matching antisubstitution proof and a constraint-extraction relation robust under later environment extensions. Separates type preservation from consistency, confluence and termination; implementation status is explicitly dated to publication.
    - limits: Underlying setting is annotated PCUIC with metavariables plus universe/sort-quality variables. Typing depends on a well-formed environment, local/metavariable contexts, structural guard conditions for fixpoint consistency and usual positivity for inductives. Virtual sort annotations matter to principal pattern types but do not carry observable matching content. Pattern matching is restricted: head of main elimination branch must be a declared symbol, not an arbitrary metavariable; variables may occur in argument holes. Patterns are left-linear, contain no β/ι-redexes, and cannot inspect syntactically irrelevant/SProp terms. Holes at irrelevant positions are allowed. These restrictions support the confluence/postponement argument. Subject reduction is conditional on appropriate confluence/triangle and pattern restrictions as well as the type-preservation criterion. Implementation of arbitrary rewrite declarations alone does not establish these global conditions. §8 says porting the Agda confluence checker is an immediate future goal. Definition4 requires a pattern-inference derivation at Tp with exactly its pattern metavariables Θ, and ordinary typing of the right side at Tp. Definition5 permits typing the right side under equalities E extracted soundly from pattern typing; it does not permit arbitrary assumptions selected to make the right side typecheck. Constraint extraction relies on rigidity/injectivity stable under environment extension. Symbols may receive future rules, so eliminations headed by symbols do not justify injective decomposition. Bare metavariable equality can be retained; equalities under higher elimination contexts are discarded, and if several equalities are extracted for one pattern variable, all but one are discarded. The full relation returning no equalities is sound but less useful. Type preservation is not consistency: symbols and rewrite principles may already be inconsistent propositionally. Consistency transfer is attributed to prior extensional-type-theory interpretation when proposed rules are admissible as propositional equalities. Justified-rules support proving this connection is future work, not required/checked automatically for every declaration. Termination is not assumed for subject reduction. The paper states a checker can be correct when it answers while potentially diverging. Its repeated decidable-criterion wording must therefore not be read as a proved total decision procedure for unrestricted user-supplied nonterminating rewrite systems. Article formally presents metatheory in the PCUIC framework and reports implementation. It does not provide a demonstrated machine-checked end-to-end proof that the modified Coq kernel implements this metatheory. No proof-checking session, kernel audit or artifact run was performed by the reader. At publication, rewrite PR18038 was integrated in development, expected for Coq8.20; type-preservation PR19290 was implemented but not yet integrated. These are historical paper statements, not checked current Coq/Rocq release status. Implementation extends presented syntax to primitive projections, universe/sort polymorphism and unfold_fix symbols. Exceptions example has acknowledged potential universe-inconsistency warnings on the if/match rules. No claim that all examples/rules are automatically safe, terminating or conservative. No runtime benchmark, corpus acceptance/rejection rate, proof-size comparison or user-study evaluation. Evidence consists of formal rules/proof arguments, counterexamples and implementation examples. Abstract formally-expressed wording is not interchangeable with fully mechanized verification.

    - what: SEV tests the Linux eBPF verifier with deterministic closed programs. It profiles accepted programs, folds their observed register states into R9, then inserts a conditional illegal operation that must be reachable under the observed execution. Accepting that transformed program exposes an unsound approximation. A one-month upstream campaign found15root-cause-distinct verifier logic bugs, including12soundness/3completeness bugs and two reported privilege-escalation cases;10were fixed at submission. This is empirical validation of a verifier, not a whole-verifier correctness proof. Records the self-checking containment oracle and paper-only argument, deterministic-input and trace-preservation assumptions, concrete folding/operator/tracer design, false-negative paths and lack of detection-equivalence proof, all bug class/location counts and overhead values, manual triage, precise sample failures/diagnostic errors and privilege conditions. Separates verified-component claims from incomplete specification/implementation correspondence and records no bugs found in tnum.c rather than treating that as proof.

The testing oracle embeds an observed value with a branch to an invalid operation; a correct analyzer must consider that branch feasible. A rejected transformed program due to the sink passes this particular test, not every state/path or full verifier soundness. §§3.1–3.2: Inputs are accepted, closed, deterministic eBPF programs without external input/interactions so a single profile is repeatable. Correct interpretation/tracing, folding evaluation and transformed control-flow/register behavior are assumed. The method does not directly validate arbitrary nondeterministic production BPF workloads, concurrent shared map changes or every environment-dependent helper. §3.1 Proposition3.1/Corollary3.1: Paper argues embedding adds no invalid operation except the sink, using branch-state partition Ai=Aj union Ak and safety under subset Ak. This is a prose argument, not a mechanized proof of the generator/transformer/verifier semantics. It presupposes correct construction and original accepted program behavior; it cannot establish that all verifier rejections are bugs without diagnosing their cause. §3.1 folded variant/§4.5: Paper calls folded detection capability equivalent to direct embedding based on likely propagation over continuous campaigns. No injectivity or detection-equivalence theorem/probability bound is proved. §4.5 explicitly allows arithmetic to hide some non-contained states. Folding collisions/precision loss and missing generated programs can produce false negatives; longer testing is not a completeness guarantee. §3.2: R9 is reserved for folded state. One random ALU function is generated per basic block, then reused each time that block occurs in a loop trace; folded expected value is evaluated in execution order. Folding excludes division and unary operations and uses nonzero registers to reduce collapse to zero. These restrictions concern folding instructions, not necessarily every original generated instruction. §3.2/§4.2: Structured generator tracks lightweight register/stack types, encodings and control flow to make accepted tests likely. Tracer records instruction indices/register states at basic blocks using an internal buffer, virtual device and mmap. It does not snapshot all accessible memory; load/store issues are detected only if they propagate to observed registers or yield another diagnosed failure. §§3.2,4.1: Interpreter bpf/core.c is patched for tracing, so runtime ground truth is relative to this interpreter/instrumentation. No claim of testing every JIT compiler, processor or architecture follows. A verifier behavior not exercised by generated accepted programs may remain unchecked. §4.1: Campaign boots compiled upstream kernels in QEMU/KVM guests, restarts dead VMs, and retains original program/profile/transformed program. Root-cause analysis/deduplication is manual; automatic discovery does not mean automatic explanation, exploit construction, patching or independent validation. §4.2: Counts are15unique roots within one month and10fixes as of submission. One final folded sink avoids that multiplication. - Verifying Peephole Rewriting in SSA Compiler IRs (2024)
    - what: LeanMLIR(X) gives intrinsically typed SSA with nested regions and user-defined operation semantics. A mechanized generic rewriter lifts local semantic equalities to whole-program equality along SSA def-use chains, with verified DCE/CSE and tactics exposing domain-level obligations. Cases cover a fragment of LLVM arithmetic, bounded structured control flow and an FHE polynomial-quotient IR. Explains typed context/variable machinery, zipper splitting/insertion and matching substitutions, structural treatment of region matches, pure-expression invariant for monadic contexts, and how operation/region signatures assemble semantics. LLVM case explicitly collapses poison and immediate undefined behavior, leaving a manual condition for division/remainder rewrites. scf generic loop laws are not all supported peephole patterns; Poly representative-dependent operations require additional choices.
    - limits: Theorems concern the user-provided embedded syntax and denotation in Lean. Kernel acceptance establishes properties of that model under its assumptions, not automatically faithful semantics of actual evolving MLIR/LLVM or a complete native compiler pipeline. Parser/elaboration errors can affect intended statement fidelity even when resulting terms are well typed. Core value semantics are pure, total Lean functions with structured regions. General unstructured CFGs, irreducible control flow, divergence, arbitrary memory effects and inter-IR linking are not fully modeled. Bounded loops are deliberately selected to avoid nontermination semantics; noncomputable algebraic denotations are allowed but not executable interpreters. Matching follows SSA expression trees and structural region equality; it does not recursively match inside regions as metavariable patterns. Rewriting can recursively visit region bodies, but free region arguments in rewrite patterns are unsupported. These are distinct capabilities. Side-effect extension only rewrites operations markedpure, denoting them in Id while other operations use an IR-specific monad. User semantics/effect classification must be appropriate. Current mechanization conservatively treats all regions as potentially effectful. LLVM instance models selected scalar arithmetic/bitwise/shift/select/icmp instructions and all comparison flags, but excludes nsw/nuw flags and most LLVM. It collapses immediateUB and poison into Option.none despite their different contextual behavior. The manual corresponding-division/remainder check is outside the mechanized collapsed-value proof. Treating UB and poison identically is safe only under an additional condition preventing a new immediateUB on the right when absent on the left. Authors report manually checking both directions for translated division/remainder rules via matching operations/arguments; this is not a proved general full-LLVM refinement theorem. Exhaustive instruction tests enumerate inputs only through bitwidth8 and use LLVM opt constant folding as ground truth. They provide empirical consistency with those cases, not proof over all widths or an independent formal LLVM semantics. Arbitrary-width rewrite proofs concern the Lean model, with some rules inherently restricted to specific widths. Alive corpus selection retains only93 of435 tests matching supported instructions and no preconditions. Automatic success54/93 and six additional selected manual proofs must not be presented as full-suite coverage or full automation. No proof times, runtime optimization speedups, hardware, repeat-count uncertainty or comparative prover-cost benchmark is provided. Poly models a pinned evolving IR’s algebra, not encryption security, ciphertext noise bounds, a complete FHE implementation or correctness of lowering quotient operations to arrays/machine code. Operations using representatives depend on a chosen section of quotient projection and need more than abstract ring laws.

    - what: Introduces a modular framework that converts width-based dynamic-programming model checkers into procedures testing graph-theoretic conjectures on bounded-width graphs. - Akshay et al. affine MDP invariants (2023)
    - title: MDPs as Distribution Transformers: Affine Invariant Synthesis for Safety Objectives.
    - what: Treats MDPs as transformers of probability distributions and synthesizes affine inductive distributional invariants together with strategies proving distribution-based safety. AlgMemLess targets memoryless strategies with relative completeness; AlgDist handles distribution-dependent general strategies with sound but incomplete Handelman-based constraints. The paper proves that distribution strategies depending only on the current distribution suffice, and that an inductive distributional invariant contained in the safe set is a sound and complete certificate. AlgMemLess templates action probabilities and a conjunction of affine inequalities, uses Farkas' lemma to eliminate universal quantifiers, and has soundness, relative completeness, and PSPACE bounds. AlgDist uses quotients of affine expressions for action probabilities; positivity constraints remove denominators, and Handelman's theorem produces a sound bounded-product translation, losing completeness. The framework handles initialized and uninitialized cases, restricted initial constraints, and can extend to polynomial invariants via Putinar's Positivstellensatz. A prototype in Python/SymPy/PySMT with Z3 and MathSAT solved Running, Chain, Split, PageRank, and Insulin-131 I examples.
    - number: AlgMemLess PSPACE, sound and relatively complete
    - number: AlgDist PSPACE for fixed K, sound but incomplete
    - number: Running 3s, 92 vars, 123 constraints
    - number: Chain 10s, 69 vars, 82 constraints

AlgMemLess is complete only relative to affine invariants and memoryless strategies; AlgDist's Handelman translation is incomplete, parameterized by product bound K, and assumes compact antecedent sets for the theorem motivation. Existential nonlinear real arithmetic is decidable but solver performance varies by orders of magnitude and can take hours. Experiments are unoptimized and small; no claim of scalability or complete decision procedure for general distribution safety is made.

- AutoHyper: Explicit-State Model Checking for HyperLTL (2023)
    - what: Presents AutoHyper, a complete explicit-state model checker for arbitrary HyperLTL quantifier prefixes, using automata quantifier elimination and practical language-inclusion backends. HyperLTL trace quantifiers are eliminated inductively into T-equivalent Büchi automata; existential elimination composes with the transition system, while universal elimination is negation plus complementation. Proposition 1 replaces the outermost complementation by inclusion L(A_T^n)⊆L(A_φ), enabling spot, RABIT, BAIT and FORKLIFT. AutoHyper is implemented in F# with symbolic alphabets and text interfaces. Experiments compare explicit-state inclusion checking with HyperQube BMC on Boolean programs, NuSMV models, SNARK linearizability, mutation tests and grid path-planning hyperproperties; it is complete and often as fast or faster. Random formulas with up to four alternations show practical growth milder than worst-case theory. A complete AutoHyper baseline quantifies strategy-based verification's incompleteness and runtime trade-offs.
    - number: On the HyperQube benchmark table, AutoHyper handles Bakery, SNARK, thread, NRP and mutation instances; HyperQube returns wrong results for Bakery3 φS3 and NRP:Tincorrect.
    - number: For grids, AutoHyper solves 60×60 shortest path in 88.83 s and robust path in 3.70 s, while HyperQube times out; 40×40 robust path takes 1.58 s versus HyperQube 265 s.
    - number: Strategy verification succeeds on 60.4% of random instances whose properties hold in 61.1% of cases.
    - number: All experiments use an Intel Core i3 Mac Mini with 16 GB RAM and spot 2.11.1 plus four inclusion backends.
    - limits: The model is finite-state, formulas are closed HyperLTL formulas over infinite traces, and explicit-state methods can exhaust the generated state space. Language inclusion remains PSPACE-complete in theory; backend performance depends on automata representation and checker. BMC may be faster on shallow cases but is incomplete for many alternated properties (for example GNI), while AutoHyper's completeness does not remove worst-case state explosion. Evaluation uses a Mac Mini i3/16GB, selected benchmark instances, fixed HyperQube bounds and semantics, and an unoptimized strategy-based engine; results may not generalize to larger systems or optimized competitors.

- Automated Verification for Real-Time Systems (2023)
    - title: Automated Verification for Real-Time Systems via Implicit Clocks and an Extended Antimirov Algorithm
    - what: Defines the core timed language C_t, the Timed Effects (TimEffs) specification logic, a Hoare-style forward verifier, and an extended Antimirov term-rewriting system (TRS) that checks timed-language inclusion. The implementation verifies source-level temporal behavior with implicit, input-dependent clocks and concurrency constructs. TimEffs combines regular-expression traces with dependent arithmetic bounds, event absence, guards, waiting, deadlines, interrupts, parallel composition and shared mutable state. Forward rules compute effect states compositionally and call the TRS at calls and postconditions; the TRS uses nullable/first/partial-derivative functions, Z3 side-condition checks, memoized reoccurrence, and explicit parallel derivatives. The paper works through addNSugar/makeCoffee and Fischer mutual exclusion, and gives a soundness theorem for the forward rules, termination and soundness theorems for the TRS, and a prototype of about 5k OCaml lines.

- AutoQ: An Automata-Based Quantum Circuit Verifier. (2023)
    - what: Presents C++ automated Hoare-style quantum-circuit checking with tree-automata sets of pure states, symbolic amplitude expressions and predicate-valued postconditions. Extends prior exact gate transformations with relational symbolic specifications and an antichain entailment procedure invoking Z3. Reports Hadamard identity, real-amplitude checks, full Grover probability checks for fixed/all encoded oracles and a weaker single-iteration amplification check, plus two injected bugs. No new machine-checked verifier correctness proof or empirical proof-writing agent is supplied. Defines symbolic-tree entailment and a compact high-level language with basis patterns, existential index and tensor products. Exact algebraic-number representation supports a finite gate set; the main new entailment step checks constraint-implied leaf predicates during bottom-up TA inclusion. Benchmark details expose how oracle quantification and weaker properties change scale and bottlenecks. Reader checks separate printed algebra/size defects from artifact correctness and distinguish the defined uniform symbolic-tree entailment from ordinary valuation-dependent set inclusion.
    - limits: Hoare input{P,phi}C{Q} has a finite OpenQASM gate sequence C, term-leaf precondition TA P, formula phi over shared symbolic values and term/predicate-leaf postcondition Q. It operates on pure-state amplitudes and unitary supported gate sequences; no measurement branching, noisy/mixed-state evolution, dynamic loops or physical-device correspondence is established. Exactness is relative to represented states and supported transformations. Each n-qubit vector is a depth-n binary decision tree, ordered by qubits, with amplitudes at2^nleaves. Tree automata share substructure and can represent all computational basis states with O(n)states/transitions. This compactness is for structured families, not a general polynomial representation of arbitrary quantum-state sets; executing gates and entailment can still grow exponentially. Introductory two-symbol construction assigns one marked amplitude vh and the same vl to every other basis. The text describes this as all states with one more probable basis, but it only covers that equal-unmarked-amplitude subclass, not arbitrary unequal lower amplitudes. A more general TA/specification may encode other structures; the displayed construction itself is restricted. High-level grammar supports fixed basis patterns with default other-basis term, existential bitstring index, finite spec unions and tensor products. Free indices, repeated bases and mixed lengths are ill-formed. Reusing an existential index across tensor factors encodes oracle/work-register relationships. This is user-authored specification automation, not automatic discovery that the postcondition captures the intended quantum algorithm. Concrete gate coefficients use(1/sqrt2)^k*(a+b*omega+c*omega²+d*omega³),integer a,b,c,d and omega=exp(i*pi/4). Supported gates:X,H,Y,Z,S,T,Rx(pi/2),Ry(pi/2),CNOT,CZ,Toffoli. This countable ring supports a universal approximation basis, not exact arbitrary-angle rotations. Solovay–Kitaev approximation for other rotations does not by itself certify the original ideal circuit/property or propagate an error budget. Precondition leaves share a normalization exponent k, omitted using normalization of the full state; relative exponent kc is tracked through gates and applied to final leaves. This depends on normalized-state/common-scale interpretation. The paper does not supply a full symbolic normalization-validation procedure or arithmetic-overflow audit. Integer symbolic terms and exact gate constants do not prove the whole C++/SMT pipeline correct. Visually confirmed formula defect on p.145: expansion first contains +c*i, but squared imaginary component is printed(b*sqrt2/2−c+d*sqrt2/2)² instead of+c. Reader example(a,b,c,d)=(0,1,1,0): |omega+i|²=2+sqrt2, whereas printed formula yields2−sqrt2. The real-amplitude condition c=0,b=−d remains valid; artifact arithmetic was not inspected and no implementation bug is inferred. Tree entailment requires each term leaf either match syntactically or satisfy phi=>postpredicate after substitution. Automaton entailment is forall source symbolic trees exists a post tree whose every leaf implication is valid under all phi-valuations. This quantifier order requires one post-tree choice uniformly across those valuations, stronger than allowing post-tree choice per concrete valuation. It is the defined check, not completeness for arbitrary extensional unions of concrete states. Reader quantifier example: identity on v|0>+(1−v)|1>,integer v∈{0,1}; postcondition is a union of predicate trees describing exactly|0> and exactly|1>. Every concrete output belongs to that union, yet neither fixed post tree matches both valuations under leafwise implication. Defined entailment can fail without a concrete physical violation under that different set interpretation. Do not treat bug found as an independently validated counterexample for every broader intended semantics. Algorithm1 initializes pairs(sourceleafstate,setofmatchingpostleafstates), combines pairs bottom-up along the same qubit label, rejects if a source root has no post root, and returns true when the worklist empties. Antichain Min/subsumption/simulation prune states; details are delegated to refs4/10. Visual line4 is Worklist!=empty; raw extraction loses the slash. Qr/Qq notation in some lines is inconsistent with Sr/Sq, not evidence of an implementation fault. C++ pipeline preprocesses .aut/.hsl/.smt/.qasm, applies imported gate transformations with symbolic leaf updates and outputs reachable TA R, then checks entailment. Uses VATA for term-only TA inclusion and Z3 for predicate implications; experiments use QF_NIRA. Allowing any Z3-supported theory is not a claim that every theory is decidable or that unknown/timeouts imply a bug. Such result handling and proof certificates are not described. Hadamard-square case uses arbitrary symbolic quadruples for both input amplitudes and phi=true, preserving each amplitude. One altered H gate is detected. Bernstein–Vazirani cases check only zero imaginary parts, not the full correct secret output, although the worked three-qubit example yields|010>. An injected BV bug violates that property. A different erroneous circuit could retain real amplitudes and evade this weaker specification. GroverSingle fixes an oracle satisfying bitstring and starts all work/ancilla bits zero; postcondition requires correct-work-basis probability>.9, other basis probabilities<.1, real amplitudes and zero ancillas. GroverAll stores an arbitrary basis-index oracle in an additional register and relates it to the work-register answer using the same index. It covers all encoded unique-solution bitstrings at a fixed n, not all Boolean functions/multiple-solution oracles or coherent superpositions of distinct oracle indices. GroverIter assumes all unmarked amplitudes are the same positive real vl, marked amplitude vh>0 and(2^n−1)*vl>vh. The postcondition increases marked magnitude and decreases every unmarked magnitude, preserves real amplitudes and zero ancillas. This avoids Grover overshoot and proves one iteration on that structured region, not overall search success for arbitrary input vectors, alliterationcounts or probability>.9. Full GroverAll reaches n9(27totalqubits),1492gates,25m16s; GroverSingle reaches n20(40qubits),141527gates,19m57s. GroverIter reaches n100(200qubits),895gates,10m53s for its weaker property.     - title: Bounded Model Checking for Asynchronous Hyperproperties
    - what: Generalizes asynchronous HyperLTL (A-HLTL) with nested trajectory quantifiers and gives a QBF-based bounded model checker for a fragment, with complexity results for acyclic Kripke structures and case-study experiments. The extended logic quantifies traces and trajectories independently, where trajectories choose which traces advance or stutter and must be fair. The bounded encoding unrolls Kripke structures to depth k and trajectory schedules to m, with pessimistic and optimistic halting semantics; Theorem 1 establishes equivalence at the structure diameter and a finite trajectory bound. - CompMDP string-diagram checking (2023)
    - title: Compositional Probabilistic Model Checking with String Diagrams of MDPs
    - what: Defines CompMDP, a compositional probabilistic model-checking algorithm for open Markov decision processes composed as string diagrams, computing optimal expected cumulative rewards while retaining reachability probabilities and scheduler alternatives. The paper formalizes open MDPs with entrances/exits, rewards, transition probabilities and almost-sure termination, then derives decomposition equalities for reachability and expected rewards under sequential composition and loops. A categorical construction builds solution functors from rightward Markov chains to MDPs and bidirectional diagrams; semantic arrows retain pairs of reachability probability and expected reward for each memoryless scheduler, with a meager subsumption optimization. CompMDP implements this in Python, supports freezing subdiagrams and delegates frozen components to PRISM, and records an optimal scheduler result. Experiments on Patrol, Wholesale and Packets test reuse, freezing and scale, including models with 10^8 positions.

The meager semantics and implementation optimization are described as correct but deferred for full categorical formalization. Sequential/task composition is better supported than parallel system composition; performance degrades with many locally optimal schedulers, low component reuse, loops, or poorly chosen freezing. - Conschecker (2023)
    - title: Optimal Stateless Model Checking for Causal Consistency
    - what: Develops a stateless model-checking framework for causal consistency variants CC, CCv and CM. The DPOR algorithm explores executions represented by program-order (po) and reads-from (rf) relations, maintaining model-specific consistency edges; it is sound, complete and optimal because each consistent po-rf trace is explored once. Conschecker implements the algorithm at LLVM IR level and reports assertion violations. The paper formally defines CC overwrite cycles, CCv conflict/arbitration cycles and CM happened-before cycles, then gives a uniform trace semantics and DPOR schedule construction. Conschecker extends Nidhugg and validates outcomes against Herd simulations. Evaluation spans 9,815 litmus tests, SV-COMP stress tests, five database applications, classical anomaly benchmarks and parameterized programs; model strength differs (e.g., Delivery Order unsafe under CC/CCv but safe under CM).

    - number: Fibonacci 6,224,342 traces/695–1,796 s
    - limits: Programs are finite-thread deterministic C programs with bounded loops, finite shared variables and atomic reads/writes; local statements are folded into transitions. The method explores terminating executions and detects user assertions, not liveness, memory safety or implementation correctness beyond the modeled semantics. Trace consistency checking can be expensive: SV-COMP examples generate millions of traces and parameterized scaling reaches 13 processes/variables in reported cases.

- continuous-time decision-tree policy safety (2023)
    - title: Safety Verification of Decision-Tree Policies in Continuous Time
    - what: Introduces the first direct continuous-time reachability algorithm for systems controlled by decision trees. It propagates set enclosures through policy branches and nonlinear ODEs, using Taylor models for dynamics and axis-aligned predicate splitting for the tree, thereby detecting between-sample safety violations. A DTCS samples a tree every control period while applying the selected action continuously. Algorithm 1 queues state sets, postT partitions them among actions, and postf computes interval and endpoint enclosures; Theorem 1 proves termination/soundness and relative completeness under exact post procedures. The implementation uses TaylorModels.jl/JuliaReach and handles fixpoints for unbounded-time results. Even state-independent dynamics f(x,u)=u yield PSPACE-complete bounded-time reach-avoid and undecidable unbounded-time reachability via reductions from LBAs and two-counter machines. Experiments distill trees from neural policies: a depth-10 six-dimensional quadrotor is verified in 6.5 minutes; cart-pole is proved safe forever by a fixpoint; acrobot policies reach goal in about 100–112s; mountain-car reaches its goal within 132 steps in 16s. A generic hybrid-automata tool stalls at bisections, showing the value of exploiting tree structure.
    - number: PSPACE-complete bounded-time and undecidable unbounded-time even for state-independent dynamics
    - number: quadrotor depth 10/177 nodes, 84s table average and 6.5min full verification
    - number: cart-pole 40s finite analysis and infinite-time fixpoint
    - number: mountain-car at most 132 steps, 16s
    - limits: Solutions to ODE initial-value problems are assumed unique; predicates are axis-aligned xi≤c; Taylor-model overapproximations and bisections can accumulate wrapping error. Fixpoint checking is for time-invariant systems and may be hard with general Taylor sets. The proof-of-concept focuses on relatively small trees and simple tasks; nonlinear reachability remains undecidable in general and exactness depends on post procedures.

- Dependently Sorted Theorem Proving for Mathematical Foundations (2023)
    - what: DiaToM is a proof-of-concept LCF-style SML prover for classical first-order logic with term-dependent sorts, formula-schema variables and a configurable equality/specification policy. Authors encode ETCS and SEAR and demonstrate proof-producing bounded comprehension translation, quotients and group homomorphisms, natural numbers/integers/lists/co-lists, a simulation-preservation characterization of modal formulas, and a set receiving injections from every finite powerset iterate of any given set. The body explains explicit context tracking for possibly empty dependent sorts, the danger of evaluating arbitrary relations as functions, specification unique up to a chosen equivalence, and proof-producing conversion from external bounded formulas to categorical internal logic. Quotient elimination requires a nonempty witness; co-list heads use option values because carriers may be empty. Concrete modal quantification and powerset-collection statements show what the chosen foundation adds, while a 2,443-line kernel and elementary SML infrastructure give qualitative implementation evidence.
    - limits: Classical first-order ambient logic; sorts s(t0,…,tn) depend on terms of earlier sorts, with each term storing its unique sort. Formula variables encode axiom schemas by instantiation, not ordinary higher-order quantified predicates. Only foundation-approved sorts support equality: no primitive object equality in ETCS or set equality in SEAR. Heterogeneous equality between differently sorted members is not expressible. Theorem Γ,A⊢φ retains all needed variables in Γ, including dependency information, so possibly empty sorts are not silently inhabited. Universal specialization adds free variables of its witness; generalization checks assumptions, sort dependencies and schema-sort lists. Substitution/matching must preserve well-formed dependent sorts; equality transport is deliberately restricted rather than a full dependent type theory. New function symbols require nonemptiness of output sorts plus unique existence modulo an equivalence with reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity proofs. Which equivalences are permitted is a foundational choice. Allowing the universal true relation imports choice. A proof-of-concept LCF architecture is reported; neither kernel implementation correctness nor consistency of newly added axioms is independently established in this paper. Semantic explanation erases sort dependencies into ordinary sorted FOL, adding domain/codomain projection functions and guarded function-symbol axioms. Quantifiers and theorem contexts gain guards. Conservative elimination of formula variables and proof-theory mechanization are reported as separate work not described here; validity of rules is sketched with universal generalization. No completeness theorem, detailed full soundness proof or metatheory artifact evaluation is supplied in this article. ETCS uses object/arrow sorts, choice and bounded internal comprehension; SEAR uses set/member/relation sorts, unrestricted formula-schema comprehension and collection, without choice as a base axiom. A new function subsort ensures Eval only accepts relations already represented as total single-valued functions. The authors call this extension conservative and cite Shulman’s personal agreement; no independent metatheory checked here. SEAR plus choice and restriction to bounded comprehension is compared in strength to ETCS. The unmodified foundations are not ordered by this sentence alone because their choice assumptions differ. The common constructions are shown in SEAR after §4; the text says ETCS analogues work except the all-model modal result and large-set construction, but does not print duplicate developments. Internalization accepts bounded formulas with appropriate element arguments and registered external/internal symbol correspondences. User-defined predicates require manually supplied correspondence theorems. It constructs a predicate arrow and a correctness theorem by derived rules, not an unchecked syntax translation or unrestricted comprehension axiom for ETCS. Quotient construction uses full equivalence relations; partial equivalences first restrict their domain. Defining a total left inverse requires a default point of the source. Empty quotient statements are handled through explicit hypotheses, not HOL’s built-in type nonemptiness. - dFHL safety architectures (2023)
    - title: Formal Verification of Safety Architectures for Automated Driving
    - what: Extends differential Floyd–Hoare logic (dFHL) with assume-guarantee Hoare quintuples and interruption/fallback constructs to prove safety envelopes and graceful degradation in automated-driving controllers. The layered simplex combines a goal-aware RSS controller with a collision-avoiding RSS fallback around a black-box advanced controller. The paper gives trace semantics for nondeterministic hybrid programs with continuous physical dynamics and environment variables, defines α↓A interruption, fallback α on β, and a two-way simplex that switches back to α. Hoare quintuples split a global assumption from a guarantee; strong and weak as-long-as/fallback rules are proved sound, and an interruption-extension discharges the weak case when an assumption fails. In the pull-over model, GA-RSS can stop at the shoulder under constant-speed POV assumptions, while CA-RSS preserves collision avoidance if POV speeds change. Margined switching conditions, counters, or timers prevent infinite controller oscillation. Simulations with a sampling-based planner answer safety, strong goal, and best-effort goal questions, including POV2 braking that interrupts and later returns control to GA-RSS.
    - number: dFHL↓ Hoare quintuples with assumptions and guarantees
    - number: three POVs in the pull-over case
    - number: ε<ε′ conservative margins
    - number: two notable POV2-braking simulations
    - limits: Proofs are conditional on explicit physical/environment assumptions (RSS distance, bounded accelerations, legal speeds, and no rear-end collision responsibility). Strong goal achievement assumes all POVs keep constant speed; when that assumption fails, the weak guarantee preserves safety but may lose the stopping goal. The advanced controller is modeled as a black box constrained only by the switching contract. Termination of a simplex requires a finite switch counter or timer construction. The case study is one pull-over geometry and a prototype planner, so it does not establish broad automated-driving coverage.

    - title: Contextuality in distributed systems
    - what: Defines a lattice of distributed-program specifications as subpresheaves of relative execution traces paired with maximal covers of a finite topological variable space. The lattice order captures refinement and parallelism; associated information algebras define local and global consistency, with global consistency related to sequential consistency. The paper constructs relative traces from nondegenerate simplicial cells of products of variable prosets, proves the trace presheaf is flasque and a tuple system, and derives an ordered adjoint information algebra of relations. Isabelle/HOL formalizes several constructions and proofs, while an explicit local-computation reformulation reduces join cost by projecting pairwise overlaps.

- Event-DPOR event-driven stateless model checking (2023)
    - title: Tailoring Stateless Model Checking for Event-Driven Multi-Threaded Programs
    - what: Introduces Event-DPOR, a dynamic partial-order-reduction algorithm for stateless model checking event-driven multithreaded programs whose handlers process mailbox messages in arbitrary order. The paper defines a finite-thread/shared-variable model with handler mailboxes, happens-before traces and trace equivalence. Event-DPOR extends Optimal-DPOR using happens-before prefixes, weak initials, wakeup trees, parked wakeup sequences and race reversal that can reorder serialized messages. Weak-initial redundancy checking is proved NP-hard; the implementation uses a sequence of inexpensive incomplete tests and a final decision procedure. Correctness proves at least one maximal execution per equivalence class; optimality proves exactly one for non-branching programs. The Nidhugg implementation stores vector clocks and handles first-conflict reversals. Benchmarks compare Event-DPOR with Optimal-DPOR, GenMC DPOR and LAPOR on posters, buyers, ping-pong, consensus, prolific, sparse-mat and plb programs.

- Finkbeiner Passing delay-dominance (2023)
    - title: Synthesizing Dominant Strategies for Liveness (Full Version)
    - what: Introduces delay-dominance, a strategy relation that compares unmatched progress failures against alternatives, to make best-effort synthesis compositional for many safety and liveness specifications. It defines a delay-dominance game, proves compositionality under an automaton bad-prefix criterion, and gives a universal co-Buchi automaton for synthesis. The paper formalizes the game where Spoiler chooses alternative-automaton branches first and Duplicator responds on the candidate strategy, proving self-dominance and that delay-dominant implies remorsefree dominant. It identifies existence of bad prefixes as the condition allowing blame of one component after composition, proves composition and winningness for realizable specifications, and constructs the recognizer by combining ACAs for phi and not-phi, Miyano-Hayashi conversion, and universal projection over alternative outputs. The resulting automaton has O(2^{|phi|^2}) states and bounded synthesis remains 2EXPTIME. Examples show immediate-send versus wait-for-peer strategies and mixed existential/universal ACA choices.

Distributed architectures use Moore process strategies and standard bounded synthesis; complexity is worst-case 2EXPTIME.

- First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Stable Graph Classes (2023)
    - what: Establishes fixed-parameter first-order model checking on every monadically stable graph class and proves monadic stability is the tractability boundary for hereditary edge-stable classes. The tractability proof first establishes almost-linear neighborhood complexity: for every ε, the number of distinct closed-neighborhood traces on a parameter set A is O(|A|^{1+ε}). A reduction using branching index, sampling and nowhere-dense machinery yields this bound. Welzl's low-crossing-number order then gives distance-r neighborhood covers of constant diameter and subpolynomial overlap via a greedy compact-interval partition; the cover can be computed in O(n^{4+ε}). Substituting it into the Flipper-game model-checking framework improves the overall bound to O_{C,ε,φ}(n^{5+ε}). For hardness, Ramsey refinement and k-flips characterize non-stability by induced subdivided cliques or webs. Careful existential “deobfuscation” yields effective interpretations of all graphs, giving AW[*]-hard FO model checking, W[1]-hard existential FO model checking, and W[1]-hard induced-subgraph isomorphism under Turing reductions.
    - number: Theorem 1 gives O_{C,ε,φ}(n^{5+ε}) model checking; neighborhood-cover construction is O_{C,r,ε}(n^{4+ε}).
    - number: Theorem 3 gives O_{C,ε}(|A|^{1+ε}) neighborhood complexity for every ε>0.
    - number: Theorem 2 gives AW[*]-hard FO, W[1]-hard existential FO, and W[1]-hard induced-subgraph isomorphism for hereditary edge-stable non-monadically-stable classes.
    - limits: The positive result assumes a fixed monadically stable graph class C and ε>0, with class-dependent constants; the hardness result assumes heredity and edge-stability. The construction handles neighborhood formulas on vertex pairs, not the stronger tuple-type bounds left as Conjecture 3. The general monadically NIP tractability conjecture remains open because suitable Flipper/decomposition machinery is unknown; the authors also state the theorem does not settle tuple neighborhoods. Hardness transfers through polynomial effective interpretations and parameterized reductions, not through an implementation benchmark. - Formalizing Results on Directed Sets in Isabelle/HOL (Proof Pearl) (2023)
    - what: Reports Isabelle/HOL proofs of Iwamura’s directed-set decomposition, equivalence of directed completeness and nonempty well-related completeness, and equivalence of Scott continuity and preservation of nonempty well-related suprema. Uses cardinal-indexed well-orders on the original carrier instead of a universal ordinal type. Generalizes from partial orders to quasi-orders and removes all codomain order/completeness assumptions in the continuity theorem. The uncountable construction closes each strict prefix under chosen finite upper bounds by countable iteration, bounding its size by the larger of the prefix size and countable infinity. Countably infinite carriers require a different finite-stage sequence; an inverse order isomorphism reconciles its natural-number index with the carrier index. Cardinal induction chooses possibly nonunique suprema of smaller directed sets, turns their monotone image into a well-related set, and transfers its supremum back to the original directed set. A strengthened simultaneous induction proves continuity for every possible supremum without assuming transitivity in the codomain.
    - limits: Directed means every finite subset, including the empty subset, has an upper bound in the carrier. Thus directed sets are nonempty. The familiar nonempty plus pairwise-upper-bound definition needs transitivity for equivalence. Iwamura’s theorem assumes reflexivity and an infinite directed carrier but does not assume transitivity; completeness and continuity equivalences assume a quasi-order, meaning reflexivity and transitivity, without antisymmetry. A well-related set is one whose every nonempty subset has a least element. This implies reflexivity but is defined without assuming transitivity or antisymmetry. A pre-well-order additionally assumes a quasi-order. In the main theorem’s quasi-ordered ambient carrier, well-related subsets inherit transitivity. Nonempty qualifiers exclude a requirement for a least element/bottom arising from an empty supremum. Choice is used to select a least-cardinality well-order of the carrier and a bound f(X) for each finite X using SOME. Later it selects a supremum for each smaller directed set. This last selection cannot use unique choice because removing antisymmetry makes suprema potentially nonunique. More constructive proof organization does not mean a choice-free or computational construction. Isabelle/HOL cannot collect arbitrarily large ordinals of every type into one ordinal type. The workaround represents an ordinal by a well-order relation and uses cardinal-library comparisons across types. The index order on A is the particular least well-order representing |A|; it is different from the original relation whose directedness is being studied. Locales permit both relations, unlike fixing one order per type through a type class. For the least well-order, every strict prefix A_prec(a) has strictly smaller cardinality. Leastness is essential: an arbitrary well-order may have a strict prefix as large as the whole carrier. An infinite least-cardinality well-order has no greatest element, since deleting one point preserves infinite cardinality. Therefore the union of all strict prefixes equals A. That equality fails for nonempty finite carriers, which are handled separately. Uncountable case: F(X)=X union {f(Y):Y is a finite subset of X}; F^omega(X) is the union of its finite iterates. Any finite set in this union is contained in one common stage, so its chosen upper bound is in the next stage. This argument needs no transitivity. F and its closure are monotone; closure stays within A and includes X. Cardinality control splits finite and infinite prefixes. A finite starting set has finite stages and at most countable closure, which is still smaller than uncountable A. For infinite X, finite subsets have the same cardinality as X, each iterate preserves that cardinality, and a countable union has size at most |X|. The proof uses existing cardinal-library lemmas; it does not assume that the original uncountable cardinal is regular. Countably infinite case: choose order isomorphism seq from natural numbers to the least well-order on A. Seq(0)={f(empty)} and Seq(n+1)=Seq(n) union {seq(n),f(Seq(n) union {seq(n)})}. Every stage is finite and directed because the added bound also bounds itself by reflexivity. This avoids countable closure becoming as large as the entire countable carrier. Compose Seq with inverse(seq) to obtain the same A-to-subsets type as the uncountable construction. Final Iwamura family is piecewise in the cardinality case; every I(a) is directed, smaller than A, nested in the chosen index order, and its union covers A. Proof locales collect definitions under directedness and are interpreted in the final theorem’s reflexive context. The printed mono_uncountable lemma uses domain D where surrounding construction uses A; the record does not infer an error in the AFP theorem from that local presentation. Reverse completeness direction: every nonempty finite subset of a well-related set has a greatest element, proved by removing a least element and inducting on finite size. This proves directedness even without transitivity. Forward direction uses cardinal induction on directed D. A finite D has a greatest element by directedness; an infinite D is decomposed by Iwamura and each smaller I(d) receives an inductively obtained supremum s(d). Monotonicity of I and of taking suprema makes s monotone from the chosen well-order on D to the original relation. A monotone image of a well-related set is well-related even without injectivity. Completeness supplies a supremum x of s(D). Covering D by I(d) and ambient transitivity shows x bounds D; any bound of D bounds each I(d), hence s(D), so x is least among bounds of D. C-continuity includes f(A) subset B and preservation of every existing supremum for each nonempty C-subset. It does not require preserving empty suprema. Under a reflexive domain and class C containing every related pair {i,j}, this property implies monotonicity. Well-related sets meet that condition, without requiring codomain reflexivity or transitivity. The continuity equivalence assumes only a quasi-ordered, nonempty-well-related-complete domain. The codomain is an arbitrary carrier and binary relation, with no reflexivity, transitivity, antisymmetry or completeness assumptions. The proof establishes completeness and preservation simultaneously by cardinal induction. It does not compose codomain inequalities through an unstated transitivity assumption. For continuity, a supplied supremum x of D may differ from the one constructed through the well-related set C. Domain transitivity proves the supplied x also is a supremum of C, so preservation applies to f(x) itself. A bound b of f(D) bounds each f(I(d)); the induction hypothesis gives f(s(d)) related to b. Thus b bounds f(C), and the least-bound property of f(x) completes the proof without codomain transitivity. Authors report 726 Isabelle lines in AFP entry Directed_Sets, plus refactoring of Complete_Non_Orders with new Continuity.thy and Directedness.thy totaling 427 lines. These counts describe different development scopes; they are not runtime or proof-success measurements. The article reports machine formalization but no build log, tactic-time statistics, independent replication, empirical benchmark or proof-agent evaluation. AFP and cited prior developments were not opened or rebuilt in this reading. The paper motivates directed sets through nets in topology, fixed-point semantics for loops and ideals in reachability/coverability of well-structured transition systems such as Petri nets. These are motivating applications, not a verified protocol, Rust implementation, Verus/TLA+ specification or applied model checker delivered here. It contains no LLM-assisted proof experiment.

    - title: Liveness Properties in Geometric Logic for Domain-Theoretic Streams
    - what: Defines LTL over the algebraic cpo of partially defined streams JStrAK and studies formula denotations through Scott topology, sobriety, frames and geometric logic. Negation-free LTL formulas translate inductively to geometric theories whose models are exactly the denotations; the paper applies the translation to prove a liveness specification for the non-productive stream filter function. The stream domain is DCPO[N,JAK] with a pointwise flat order, so finite-support streams are compact approximants and total streams are their directed suprema. The authors prove negation-free denotations are upward-closed and induce sober subspaces, while negation can destroy sobriety (e.g., J¬□aK excludes aω). They stratify negation-free LTL into G, Gδ and full fragments, define geometric-formula operators for next/until/weak-until, and prove model equivalence (Theorem 3). A frame/deduction treatment establishes spatiality for countable theories and gives complete deduction for Gδ formulas. For filter, ordinary fixpoint induction fails because the bottom function does not satisfy total-output liveness; finite-occurrence formulas ψn,k and output approximants φk yield Lemma 13 and prove that infinitely many predicate-satisfying input elements imply a total filtered stream.

    - title: Quantitative Safety and Liveness
    - what: Generalizes safety, liveness, the safety-progress hierarchy, and safety-liveness decomposition from Boolean properties to quantitative trace properties over complete lattices. It defines quantitative safety/liveness by finite-prefix rejection of threshold hypotheses, proves closure/decomposition theorems, and derives finite-state approximate monitors for properties that are approximately safe and co-safe. The paper introduces quantitative properties Φ:Σ^ω→D over complete lattices, quantitative safety via finite witnesses for wrong lower-bound hypotheses, and the safety closure Φ*(f)=inf_{s≺f} sup_g Φ(sg). It proves safety iff upper semicontinuity iff equality with safety closure, safety iff inf-property, co-safety iff sup-property, and characterizes lim-inf/lim-sup levels. New liveness and co-liveness definitions are shown to generalize Boolean liveness; every property decomposes as min(Φ*,Ψ) with Ψ live, and as the minimum of two live properties. Approximate α-safety/β-co-safety are characterized by closure gaps; for real-valued limit properties these imply suffix influence eventually falls below any δ>α+β, yielding a finite-state (δ,δ)-monitor. Examples include minimal/maximal/average response times and discounted safety.

- LISA – A Modern Proof System (2023)
    - what: Initial proof assistant and kernel for single-sorted schematic first-order logic with equality and axiomatic set theory. Kernel uses ortholattice-based formula comparison, explicit DAG proof steps and theory-specific sealed theorem values. Scala DSL constructs checked proofs/tactics; demonstrations include a propositional solver, unique/underspecified definitions and Cantor’s theorem. Explains which propositional equivalences and limited quantifier rules the efficient kernel handles, why automatic quantifier instantiation is excluded from F(OL)^2 comparison while explicit instantiation proof steps remain kernel-checkable, how standalone proof imports differ from justified theory theorems, and why schematic axiom schemas make existence-only definition unsound as a conservative extension. Schematic symbols are not bound higher-order quantifiers; authors argue they do not increase expressive power because instantiation can be simulated. No proof of consistency of ZFC/Tarski-Grothendieck axioms is supplied. Kernel implementation is about 1607 Scala lines of code, with about 300 for the ortholattice algorithm. Polynomial/quadratic complexity claims concern checking explicit proof data and formula comparisons, not general proof search. No machine-checked verification of the whole Scala kernel/compiler/runtime or empirical complexity benchmark is reported. Ortholattice equivalence is a restricted propositional theory excluding Boolean distributivity. F(OL)^2 extends it with equality symmetry/reflexivity, universal monotonicity and congruence for schematic connectors. It is not a complete validity or equivalence decision procedure for first-order logic. Standalone proof checking establishes derivability from explicitly listed imports; it does not prove imported axioms/theorems themselves. Theory validates imports against its own stored axioms/theorems/definitions, and a theorem remains relative to that theory’s assumptions. Calling the result unconditionally true in the paper does not establish consistency of arbitrary user axioms. Theorem type depends on a specific Theory instance; host language path-dependent types prevent ordinary mixing of facts from distinct theories. Scala type checking is a usability/encapsulation mechanism, while kernel proof checking remains the proof-validity boundary. Function definitions require fresh symbol and proof of unique existence. Existence alone could yield a global pick function and Choice when new symbols are usable in replacement schemas. Underspecification weakens the exposed fact after checking a unique construction; it does not discard the existence/uniqueness obligation. Tautology is a non-clausal DPLL-like propositional proof search with worst-case exponential atom branching, most-frequent-atom heuristic and ortholattice simplification. It defines memoryless and history-dependent uniform strategies and natural guarded-action strategies, including epistemic conditions and regular-expression recall. Tables give concrete complexity classifications: ATL is PTIME-complete with perfect information but undecidable with imperfect information and memoryful strategies; ATL* is PSPACE-complete memoryless and 2EXPTIME-complete perfect-information memoryful, while imperfect-information memoryful is undecidable; SL is PSPACE-complete imperfect-information memoryless and non-elementary perfect-information memoryful. The review argues memoryless strategies are weak, memoryful strategies are costly, and natural-strategy complexity and imperfect-information taxonomies remain open.

- Neural Activation Patterns as Specifications (2023)
    - title: Towards Reliable Neural Specifications
    - what: Proposes neural representation as specification: mine partial neural activation patterns (NAPs) shared by most examples of a class, then verify classification and robustness for the whole input region following that pattern. A relaxation factor δ controls precision/recall. NAPs can be encoded directly in Marabou, support non-ambiguity checks between labels, and augment input norm-balls to verify larger regions. The method’s mining algorithm counts neuron activation frequencies on class training data, selecting activated/deactivated neurons above δ and below 1−δ. The paper distinguishes NAP robustness (all inputs following a pattern are classified as the label) from NAP-augmented robustness (norm-ball intersected with the pattern region). Controlled 2-D visualization explains why activation regions are flexible and larger than boxes. VNNCOMP-21 MNIST and CIFAR10 experiments quantify precision/recall, timeouts, coverage and robustness bounds; δ=0.99 yields an MNIST digit-1 NAP covering 84% of test images and verifies ε=0.3 for six of seven previously non-robust inputs. CIFAR10 verifies some examples at ε=0.12 (10× the prior bound) when δ=0.9.

    - title: Petrification: Software Model Checking for Programs with Dynamic Thread Management
    - what: Reduces verification of dynamically forked/joined concurrent programs to fixed-thread Petri programs. Petrification instantiates at most β thread copies, separates control flow from data, and adds safety and bound specifications; iterative β increases detect semantic thread width. The Conc semantics permits non-unique thread IDs and sequentially consistent arbitrary interleavings. Petrification renames local variables per template/instance, adds inUse/notInUse/insuff places, and labels Petri transitions with assignments and guards. Code executes only on init/packet arrival; timers must be checked within handler. Capability allocation only at initialization and may fail externally, e.g.OOM. Failed checking can be incompleteness/threshold/timeout rather than an actual implementation bug. §3.4: Unknown-item invariant applies only to unknown keys, not every known item; equality consistency handles aliases and KnownSize constrains distinct present known keys. Map layers share base unknown state and lazily transform known entries so later reads on old/new versions remain related. Ordered queues/stacks are expressible but authors believe poorly suited to inference. §4: Candidate constraints from initialized/known items are relaxed until inductive over each packet path; cross-map FK,FV,FP functions are discovered from known items and checked against unknown invariants. A kernel-acceptance bug needs an explicit observable test symptom, not merely a generic compiler error oracle. - Automating cutoff proofs (2022)
    - title: Automating and Mechanizing Cutoff-based Verification of Distributed Protocols
    - what: Formalizes cutoff-based verification for parametric distributed protocols in the Relational Modeling Language (RML). A finite cutoff instance is sufficient when every safety violation in any larger instance can be simulated by a trace of the cutoff; the paper encodes this simulation in first-order logic and uses SMT to check it. The paper gives initial, step, and safety simulation conditions and a first-violation refinement that removes the need to simulate behavior after a violation. A backward static analysis starts from instantiated negated safety clauses, follows action updates into guards to a fixed point, and emits the relevant action set, simulation relation, and lockstep. In the sharded key-value example, the analysis reduces eight actions to four and proves a two-node cutoff. The implementation checks the formulas with Z3 and handles seven protocols: four cutoffs are synthesized automatically; three require small manual changes. Two-phase commit exposes a limit: universally quantified guards force actions of all larger-instance nodes into the simulation, requiring an extra failure-simulating node and constraints.

    - number: 4/7 automatic synthesis; 3/7 small manual changes
    - number: 20–40 ms per protocol
    - number: 2-node sharded-key-value cutoff
    - limits: RML domains are finite per instance but may have infinitely many valid interpretations; safety properties are assumed universally quantified. The result is for safety, not liveness. Cutoff correctness depends on a simulation relation for every valid larger interpretation and on a safe finite cutoff. Automatic synthesis can fail when universal guards or side effects conflict, as in two-phase commit, and the basic key-value store needs an added precondition.

    - what: Introduces BlueCov, a Java bytecode coverage tool that consumes JBMC’s own coverage goals, instruments exactly those bytecode locations, records runtime hit counts and feeds uncovered goals back to JBMC for incremental test generation. - OCTAL LTL graph learning (2022)
    - title: OCTAL: Graph Representation Learning for LTL Model Checking
    - what: Introduces OCTAL, a graph-representation-learning approach that classifies whether a Büchi automaton satisfies an LTL formula. It represents the automaton as a bipartite graph, the formula as an expression tree, joins matching variables, and trains GNNs to avoid explicit negated-formula automaton and product construction. Section 3 specifies graph construction, NNF formula normalization, shared variable/negation node encoding, and a unified graph C. A 3-layer GIN performs message passing and mean pooling for binary classification. Section 4 builds Short (9,424), Diverse (6,107), and RERS19 (1,798) datasets, compares OCTAL GIN/GCN against MLP, LinkPredictor and LTL3BA, tests domain shift and one-vs-many ranking, and drops graph edges to assess robustness. Appendix experiments cover directed graphs and encodings.

Removing all edges collapses performance near random; graph preprocessing overhead is substantial. Authors position it as a first-line filter with traditional model checking for confirmation.

- pCTL-REBEL lifted relational model checking (2022)
    - title: Lifted Model Checking for Relational MDPs
    - what: Introduces pCTL-REBEL, a lifted probabilistic model checker for relational Markov decision processes that reasons over first-order abstract states instead of grounding all objects, and proves decidability for state-bounded infinite domains via finite abstract RMDPs and probabilistic bisimulation. The paper defines OI-subsumption relational states, grounding semantics, relational pCTL including next and bounded/unbounded until, and a relational Bellman operator whose V and Q rules store probabilities rather than rewards. Logical regression, Q-rule combination, V-rule maximization and three mutually recursive Check/CheckUntil/CheckNext algorithms implement lifted checking, including absorbing goals and state-bound filtering. Theorem 1 proves that an abstract RMDP for a state-bounded infinite model is probabilistically bisimilar for a formula, so checking the finite abstraction is equivalent to checking the infinite MDP. Worked blocks-world regressions and nested formulas expose rule construction. The unoptimized SWI-Prolog prototype checks infinite blocks/box worlds and compares against PRISM/STORM; pCTL-REBEL handles 15 blocks (6.6e13 ground states) under 1800 seconds while PRISM explicit handles 8 and STORM sparse 9, but indefinite-horizon checking grows exponentially and road-map constraints cause runtime explosions.

- Red Belly holistic verification (2022)
    - title: Holistic Verification of Blockchain Consensus
    - what: Parameterized model checking verifies binary Byzantine consensus associated with Red Belly Blockchain under n>3t and0≤f≤t. First verifies binary-value broadcast, then substitutes a smaller specification-based automaton into the outer consensus and checks safety and progress properties with ByMC. Agreement and validity do not require the added good-round fairness; termination does. The verified algorithm is the coordinator/timeout-free pseudocode variant under that fairness, rather than a proof of the deployed implementation or its partial-synchrony mechanism. Makes the decomposition concrete: global sent-message counters replace local receive counts; Byzantine effects lower enabling thresholds by f; four temporal broadcast properties support a replacement gadget; round communication closure reduces selected all-round LTL obligations to one-round checking. Manual meta-arguments connect per-superround invariants to global agreement/validity and good-round existence to eventual decision. Gives a fair-round definition, a nonterminating4-process trace, detailed automaton rules, explicit liveness preconditions and measured schema counts.
