- DryVR: Data-Driven Verification and Compositional Reasoning for Automotive Systems. (2017)
    - what: Combines black-box continuous simulators with white-box acyclic timed switching graphs. Learns exponential sensitivity bounds from sampled trajectory pairs, bloats simulations into reachable-state enclosures and refines initial/switching intervals. Provides trace-containment and sequential-composition arguments for extending selected bounded analyses. Reports five safe/three unsafe automotive benchmark configurations and two composition/containment illustrations. Correctness is conditional on learned functions actually being universal discrepancy bounds; sampled validation does not establish that premise. Defines graph/trajectory/hybrid semantics, sample-to-linear-program sensitivity learning, topological enclosure propagation and conditional safety. Separates polynomial sufficient graph simulation from general timed trace inclusion and gives an inductive repeated-composition closure theorem. Complete learning protocol/table/resource details expose the gap between empirical point coverage and universal verification. Reader counterexample refutes the printed generic separator sample bound and identifies formula/pseudocode defects without inferring implementation bugs.
    - limits: Finite modes and a directed acyclic transition graph with nonnegative closed bounded dwell-time intervals. Repeated modes are permitted at different vertices; cycles require bounded unfolding. Thus a graph describes finitely many switches within bounded time, not arbitrary unconstrained switching. Intervals are durations in current mode, not absolute global timestamps. Continuous trajectory sets are deterministic and prefix-closed, with connected compact initial domains and existence over every finite horizon. At a mode switch the next trajectory starts at the preceding final state: no reset map is modeled. Mode-local time constraints support settling requirements measured since last transition. Physical fidelity of the Simulink model and mode/initial/unsafe specification remains assumed. Execution ends with a terminal mode label and no terminal-mode trajectory. It does not analyze arbitrary evolution after arrival at that label. Reachability formula allows i=k although tau_k is absent, so terminal reach needs an endpoint convention; composition prose uses final arrival states. The terminal case and final-state projection are presentation assumptions rather than an inspected implementation semantics. Definition4 assumes perfect simulation values equal true trajectory samples; validated simulations are proposed as an alternative. MATLAB numerical solver use in experiments is not by itself proof of that assumption or a validated enclosure for every inter-sample point. Imported reach-bloating machinery and numerical error treatment were not independently audited. A discrepancy beta must bound all same-mode trajectory-pair distances and vanish as initial states coalesce. GED is norm(x1−x2)*K*exp(gamma*t). Logdistance/time samples give linear inequalities in gamma,lnK; LP minimizes gamma*T+lnK. Identical initial points or zero later distance require limiting/exclusion conventions for logarithms. Neither finite pairs nor sampled times establish the universal continuous-time premise without additional assumptions. Proposition4 prints k>=epsilon^(-1)*ln(delta^(-1)) for any feasible sampled separator. Its proof treats the bad set B of the data-selected separator as fixed. Reader counterexample: Gamma={(y²,y):0<=y<=1}, uniform y, true separator x<=1. With k=2 choose sampled chord a=y1+y2,b=−y1*y2, feasible on both samples. Its error is1−abs(y1−y2). For epsilon=.5,delta=.4,k2 satisfies the printed bound, yet probability(error>.5)=.75>.4. This refutes the stated generic feasible-learner guarantee/proof, not PAC learning generally and not necessarily a separately analyzed specific LP selection. Even a valid distributional PAC bound would constrain probability mass of missed pairs/time points rather than prove every trajectory satisfies beta. Correlated pairs/times, multiple learned modes, refined initial distributions, repeated calls and continuous-time interpolation need separate sampling/union/error arguments; these budgets are absent. Theorem1 explicitly assumes every returned beta is a valid discrepancy, and therefore cannot turn the reported test fraction into universal soundness. PED partitions time adaptively to keep gamma_i<2. Printed local condition uses exp(gamma_i*t) rather than elapsed local time, and displayed chained bound has only one K. Multiplying separate local bounds with K would normally introduce K^i as well as appropriate shifted times; global normalization/K=1 or another derivation is needed. The printed norm expression also has equality instead of subtraction in places. These are presentation/derivation issues; actual code not inspected. GraphReach topologically processes initial enclosures, learns beta per vertex/enclosure, bloats finite simulations and restricts the reach tube to each outgoing dwell interval as a successor initial enclosure. Multiple incoming sets can coexist. All states/times must be enclosed for safe-disjointness. Algorithm1 computes max over outgoing labels even for a terminal vertex, where that set is empty; terminal skipping/zero-time handling is unstated. VerifySafety partitions initial sets and refines initial/switching intervals on ambiguous overlap. Printed line3 calls GraphReach(H) after popping S without setting H.initial=S, although prose clearly intends analysis from S.     - what: Builds a reusable Isabelle/HOL framework that formalizes strong eventual consistency (SEC), an asynchronous unreliable causal-broadcast network, and three operation-based CRDTs: Replicated Growable Array, Observed-Remove Set, and increment-decrement Counter. The abstract convergence theorem proves that distinct happens-before-consistent operation lists with the same set of operations yield the same state when concurrent operations commute, while a separate no-failure condition gives progress. The network locale has six axioms covering unique node histories, delivery cause, local delivery, globally unique message IDs, causal delivery, and valid broadcast operations; messages may be delayed, reordered, dropped, or nodes may crash permanently. RGA proof models immutable element IDs, tombstones, insertion ordering, causal validity, and proves concurrent operations commute and application never fails. ORSet uses add IDs and remove sets of observed IDs; Add/Remove commute only under a proved independence condition. Counter operations commute unconditionally. The framework is executable via Isabelle code generation; one counter implementation ran over TCP, but detailed performance/fault-tolerance evaluation was left for future work.

An unravelling algorithm explores forward/backward tracks with this bound, and recursive Check/ModCheck procedures are proved sound and complete. Examples encode scheduler mutual exclusion, reachability, and starvation; hardness reductions establish PSPACE-hard AABE/AB and coNP-hard propositional fragments.

For a VPS, the model-checking automaton simulates states along the cardinal branch and verifies guessed matching-return states in nested subtrees. - Automaton learning for infinite safety games (2016)
    - title: An Automaton Learning Approach to Solving Safety Games over Infinite Graphs.
    - what: Learns finite-state winning controllers for safety games over infinite or very large graphs. Rational arenas encode vertex sets as regular languages and edges as rational relations; an ICE-like teacher returns positive, negative, existential-implication or universal-implication counterexamples, and a SAT-based learner constructs minimal consistent DFAs. The paper proves closure properties of rational relations, defines winning sets and a generic automata-theoretic teacher, and gives SAT encodings whose satisfiability is equivalent to existence of an n-state DFA consistent with the sample. The minimal-consistent-DFA algorithm increments n and terminates at the minimum; the full learner terminates with a winning set when one exists. An RPNI heuristic is sound but incomplete and restricted to finite out-degree. Examples include unary encodings of grid positions, implication counterexamples, diagonal/box/evasion/follow games and program repair.

    - what: Introduces FACT, which computes statistically valid confidence intervals for PCTL and reward properties of parametric discrete-time Markov chains whose unknown transition probabilities are estimated from transition counts.     - title: Limit-Deterministic Büchi Automata for Linear Temporal Logic
    - what: Gives a direct compositional translation from full LTL to limit-deterministic Büchi automata (LDBA). A nondeterministic initial component tracks after-formulas and guesses eventually true G-subformulas; a deterministic accepting component uses breakpoint G-monitors and auxiliary monitors to check the guess. The construction supports the standard quantitative MDP model-checking algorithm by encoding jumps as product actions. The construction defines Reach(ϕ) via the after-function modulo propositional equivalence, then builds one deterministic G-monitor for each guessed G-subformula and a product of monitors, plus an auxiliary monitor for the G-free residual. Stable sets characterize which G-subformulas eventually hold; Lemmas 4–8 establish monitor/product correctness and Theorem 1 proves language equivalence. Theorem 2 gives a double-exponential lower bound. Theorem 3 proves that the LDBA can be used directly in quantitative MDP checking by delaying the jump until a BSCC determines the eventual G-set. Optimizations remove sinks/transient jumps and simplify monitor states.

- Parsimonious, Simulation Based Verification of Linear Systems (2016)
    - what: Computes reachable sets for affine linear, possibly time-varying ODEs from n+1 validated simulations for n-dimensional state space. Generalized star sets retain an arbitrary coefficient predicate while advancing a center and basis vectors, allowing nonconvex and unbounded initial sets, sound safety proofs, and sound unsafety witnesses. Superposition makes the exact time-t image a basis transformation with the coefficient predicate unchanged (Algorithm 1, Theorem 1). Algorithm 2 uses synchronized convex enclosures of center/basis trajectories; existential formulas overapproximate the union of reachable states across a time interval, while universally quantified enclosures with existential coefficients underapproximate even the intersection across that interval (Theorem 2 proof). Only m+1 simulations are needed for m basis vectors. For normalized bounded polyhedral/ellipsoid coefficients, Theorem 3 gives a 3ε bloating bound enabling efficient LP checks. General predicates need bilinear reasoning and quantified real formulas. The hybrid extension applies guards, invariants and linear resets through a mode queue. Simulations can be reused for multiple initial predicates sharing the same center/basis. The implementation combines ODEINT fourth-order Runge-Kutta with separate rigorous error bounds, GLPK for polyhedra and Z3 quantifier elimination for general initial sets.

    - what: Introduces RAHFT, a modular CHC safety verifier combining constraint specialization, convex-polyhedra abstract interpretation, finite-tree-automata trace abstraction refinement and SMT feasibility checks. It returns safe, unsafe or an abstract counterexample and can be reconfigured to use each component separately. The abstraction module specializes clauses without unfolding, computes a convex-polyhedra fixed point containing at most one constrained fact per predicate, and records derivation traces as an FTA. A verifier accepts an inductive model or selects an abstract false trace; infeasible traces are generalized by interpolant automata. The refinement module computes FTA difference via optimized determinization, then generates equisatisfiable refined clauses that split predicates, so previous refinements need not be retained. - Adam (2015)
    - title: Adam: Causality-Based Synthesis of Distributed Systems
    - what: Presents the Adam Java implementation of symbolic Petri-game synthesis: a separate controller for each process uses its causal past and exchanges knowledge at joint transitions. A winning strategy avoids bad places and avoids introducing deadlocks. The paper sketches a finite two-player reduction and reports controller-synthesis benchmarks. Cuts are maximal concurrent sets of places annotated by enabled decision sets and type-1/type-2 system tokens. Type-2 tokens will never synchronize, even indirectly, with the environment; type-1 tokens are blocked until its next move. Environment choices are delayed until an mcut so independent system choices cannot depend on unseen environment choices. The BDD encoding assigns places to tokens rather than arbitrary subsets of places. Phase 1 computes valid type-2 cuts by greatest fixed point; phase 2 combines greatest/least fixed points for winning mcuts and their predecessors; phase 3 extracts a strategy and per-player projections. Net invariants compact the place encoding.

These are finite-state model results, not parameterized proofs over arbitrary process counts. §3.1 Definition2: alternation-free means one quantifier type in negation normal form plus placement restrictions: no existential in the left of Until or right of Release; no universal in the right of Until or left of Release. Boolean combinations of separately checked blocks are handled. A formula with no textual ∀/∃ switch can still incur extra alternation through a forbidden temporal placement. §3.1: standard Boolean/Next/Until/Release automata are combined bottom up. Existential path elimination first applies Miyano–Hayashi nondeterminization, then products with the Kripke structure and projects a state component. This preserves a common witness path across alternating branches; projecting arbitrary alternating branches independently is not the construction. §3.1 Theorem2 states PSPACE-completeness in formula size and NLOGSPACE-completeness in explicit Kripke-structure size. This is not a logarithmic-space or polynomial-time claim in the number of circuit latches: a circuit represents an exponentially large state graph. Proposition1 gives correctness with structural-induction explanation; no mechanized metatheory or verified implementation is supplied. §3.2: full logic uses complementation of alternating automata and nondeterminization. With g(0,n)=n and g(k,n)=c^g(k-1,n), Theorem4 gives NSPACE(g(k,|formula|)) and NSPACE(g(k-1,|K|)), defining level-1 as NLOGSPACE. These are upper bounds parameterized by alternation depth; the practical circuit implementation/evaluation is for the restricted alternation-free fragment. §4: circuit transition is input-enabled and input-deterministic, with nonempty initial states. Associated Kripke structure adds a dummy initial state and shifts atoms by Next. Strong-fairness pair(a1,a2) requires a1 finitely often or a2 infinitely often. Validity is reduced to an initial formula output, no bad outputs and these fairness conditions; plain bounded safety search is not a complete substitute for fair reachability. §4 Proposition3 bounds latch count by |C|*k+|formula| for k path quantifiers; the paper defines circuit size as number of latches, abstracting the gate list. This does not bound every gate/transition-expression size by the same expression. Quantifier copies synchronize their starting latches; outputs track obligations and bad-state violations. Conjunction/Release circuit rules are explicitly omitted for space; correctness is sketched by structural induction. §5: implementation transforms AIGER circuits obtained by standard VHDL/Verilog synthesis; ABC supplies IC3/PDR, interpolation and BMC. Failure alone is not a security vulnerability. NI3 holds with write enable off; NI5 fails because concurrent masters/arbitration affect later interpretation. Long-term NI7/8 fail, indicating information may persist. NI6 is listed/timed but has no separate prose explanation. §5.1: 3-bit address flow is determined for QNI1, while the log2(9)≈3.17-bit upper-bound query QNI2 times out. Neither quantitative-flow query is in Table1. Illegal select IDs advance process0. Excluding those paths, parameterizing tie resolution and contracting ID comparisons into one step change assumptions/model behavior before S3 is satisfied. Results do not show the unchanged original protocol is fully symmetric or prove starvation freedom/mutual exclusion under every scheduler. §5.2: printed S1–S3 use two universal path quantifiers, despite prose saying every execution has another swapped execution. Deterministic input-enabled circuit semantics support relating paired swapped inputs; do not silently rewrite the displayed formula to ∀∃. The weak-until rewrite removes a liveness-shaped part only under the stated input-determinism/input-enabledness conditions. §5.3: valid encoder properties depend on reset/control configuration and distinct data inputs. Huffman and8b10b are not error-correcting codes and only distance1 is expected. Hamming7–4 encodes4bits into7bits and is checked up to distance3. - Automated and Modular Refinement Reasoning for Concurrent Programs (2015)
    - what: Introduces civl, a Boogie extension that proves multi-layer refinement of concurrent shared-memory programs. Cooperative yield semantics, mover-type automata, location invariants, linear permissions and modular ownership reduce preemptive concurrency reasoning to automated per-procedure obligations. A high-level atomic action is refined by a procedure whose paths contain exactly one implementing atomic block; other blocks preserve visible state. Mover types and the yield sufficiency automaton justify cooperative reasoning for sequentially consistent preemptive execution. Linear variables guarantee distinct thread identifiers or disjoint permission sets across threads. Location invariants are checked for sequential correctness and non-interference; modules own disjoint globals so quadratic checks are per module. A soundness theorem chains layers from safe high-level program to low-level implementation. Implementation infers verification conditions and atomic blocks, computes graph simulations in O(n·m), and supports variable hiding/data refinement.

- Differential radical invariants (2014)
    - title: Characterizing Algebraic Invariants by Differential Radical Invariants
    - what: Characterizes invariant algebraic varieties of polynomial vector fields using a finite chain of successive Lie derivatives of one polynomial. The resulting differential-radical invariant rule is sound and complete for checking invariance over real-closed fields, and generation reduces to maximizing the kernel dimension (equivalently minimizing rank) of a symbolic matrix. Defines the Zariski closure of an ODE orbit as the smallest algebraic overapproximation, proves its soundness and differential-ideal property, and establishes the differential radical characterization theorem: h vanishes on an orbit iff finitely many Lie derivatives vanish initially. Theorem 2 gives a decidable invariant-variety check and a sound/complete proof rule; Theorem 3 says every invariant variety is a differential-radical ideal of one polynomial. Homogenization converts generation to biaffine symbolic linear algebra; Gaussian elimination searches parameter assignments and Proposition 3 gives a sound orbit overapproximation condition. Case studies recover trigonometric identities, airplane collision invariants, and three longitudinal-aircraft energy functions.

Generation is at least NP-hard and PSPACE under stated no-parameter assumptions; de-homogenization may fail for projective candidates. - Regression-Free Synthesis for Concurrency. (2014)
    - what: Defines concurrency repair that preserves sequential behavior and, when initially correct, complete preemption-free behavior, while eliminating assertion errors. Adds constraints learned from good traces to the constraints learned from counterexamples, aiming to prevent a repair from breaking previously good behavior. Names the generic positive-and-counterexample extension to CEGIS PACES. §2 precisely relates traces before and after adjacent within-basic-block instruction swaps or atomic-section insertion. A regression must preserve reads-from relationships into assume/await conditions and must originate from a good trace that could not already become bad by scheduler choices alone. §3 uses trace-analysis graphs with intra-thread, reads-from-conditional/assertion and non-free write-order edges. A cover proves the necessary happens-before edge; additional noninterference edges place other writes before the source write or after the read. Conjoining/disjoining cover constraints yields a polynomial-time sufficient regression-prevention algorithm; when no cover exists, the theoretical fallback fixes every current intra-thread order. Exact sound-and-complete constraints can be computed exponentially. Bad-trace elimination reuses partial-order generalization and cycle constraints from the 2013 predecessor. §4 maintains cumulative constraints and good-trace images as the program changes, formalizing correspondence more carefully than scheduler input reuse. Wait/notify repair is discussed for inputs outside the standard sequential-correctness precondition.

- The Formalization of Decision-Free Petri Net (2014)
    - what: Reports a Mizar-library formalization of decision-free Petri nets, alternating directed paths and simple circuits, natural-valued markings, enabled transitions and totalized firing. Proves that each circuit’s sum of place tokens is preserved by a transition and by every finite sequence under that firing operation. Separates genuinely firable sequences from total evaluation, where disabled transition attempts leave the marking unchanged. The decision-free condition requires exactly one incoming and one outgoing transition per place, not one input/output per transition. A key structural lemma shows that any transition incident to a circular path’s place must occur on that path. Alternating-position and almost-injective-sequence lemmas support the one-step circuit invariant, which extends to finite sequences through the firing composition law. Firing is explicitly a no-op when disabled, so the final theorem needs no enabled-sequence premise; this strengthens the total-function equality without establishing legal execution or liveness.
    - limits: Markings map places to natural numbers. Arcs are unweighted relations in the displayed definitions: a successful firing subtracts one at input-only places, adds one at output-only places, and leaves both/neither places unchanged. No timed transitions, capacities, inhibitor arcs, arc weights, failure model or scheduling fairness appear in this formalization, despite reference [19] being a timed-Petri-net textbook. Decision-free-like (Definition 7) says every place has exactly one predecessor transition and exactly one successor transition. A transition may have multiple input or output places. The final decision-free-net mode also assumes Petri-like and existence of a directed circuit. Underlying Petri-like/basic-net definitions are imported and not expanded in the article; this reading does not independently audit those MML definitions. Directed paths have odd length at least three, alternate place-to-transition and transition-to-place arcs, and end at a place. Circuits additionally are circular and almost one-to-one: they close at the first place without internal repetitions. The repeated endpoint is not counted twice, since token sums use the finite set of places in the sequence, not the sequence with multiplicities. Preliminaries define an enumeration of marking values on a finite place subset and sum it to obtain the token number. Empty subsets use the empty sequence. The paper also establishes finite-sequence uniqueness facts and a smallest example PN0 with place 0, transition 1 and both connecting arcs. It does not provide a new algorithm for finding every circuit in a large net. Propositions 5–10 locate initial/final arcs and show places occur at odd indices and transitions at even indices, with neighboring arcs around each internal occurrence. Proposition 15 uses unique per-place predecessors/successors to show that a transition incident to any place of a circular path is a transition of that path. Without that closure, a transition outside the circuit could inject or remove a circuit token. A transition is firable exactly when all its input places have positive token counts (Definition 11). Definition 12 makes firing total: if firable, update by incidence; otherwise return the original marking. Input-output self-loops still require a positive token even though their net update is zero. Disabled attempts are stuttering evaluations, not enabled transitions. Definition 13 separately defines a firable finite sequence using a chain of intermediate markings and an enabledness obligation at every position; the empty sequence qualifies. Definition 14 evaluates any finite transition list using the total one-step Firing function and returns the initial marking for an empty list. Its absence of enabledness conditions is deliberate in the displayed definition and determines the scope of Proposition 17. Propositions 11/12 connect a transition with its singleton list and their firability. Proposition 13 gives Firing(Q concatenated Q1,M)=Firing(Q1,Firing(Q,M)) without a firability premise. Proposition 14 derives prefix firability and suffix firability at the prefix result from firability of the concatenation; no converse is stated in the printed proposition. Proposition 16 quantifies over a decision-free net, one circuit, any natural marking and any transition. It preserves the sum over exactly that circuit’s place set. Proposition 17 extends this equality to any finite transition sequence, with no assumption that the sequence is firable. It does not establish global conservation of all places, boundedness of every place in an arbitrary net, liveness, deadlock freedom, fairness, reachability completeness or infinite-trace properties. Reader proof explanation: a disabled transition stutters. A transition disjoint from the circuit changes no circuit place. If it touches the circuit, Proposition 15 puts it on the circuit; almost injectivity and unique place incidence leave one circuit input and one circuit output (possibly the same place). Thus the one-step sum change is zero, and finite-sequence iteration preserves it. The article gives dependency lists rather than a complete displayed Mizar proof script for the final two propositions. The article identifies MML entry PETRI_DF, version 8.1.02 5.22.1199, and supplies formal theorem statements with short proofs/dependency references. This is evidence of a published formalized development, not an independent local check. No MML files, proof checker, executable simulator, benchmark, empirical protocol case study, proof-time measurements or artifact build was run or inspected here. The paper has no Verus, verified Rust, TLA+ or LLM-agent result. Its relevance is reusable transition-system invariants and precise enabledness semantics. Applying its invariant to a distributed protocol would require a proved model relation from protocol states/steps to this restricted net class. A claim that a resource count is preserved in deployed code would need that extra refinement argument.

    - title: Two Variable vs. Linear Temporal Logic in Model Checking and Games
    - what: Compares two-variable first-order logic (FO2) and linear temporal logic (LTL), including unary temporal logic UTL, stutter-free fragments, and the combined FO2[LTL]. Translation I relates UTL/FO2 to unambiguous limit-deterministic Büchi automata; Translation II exploits polynomially many FO2[<] subformula types under a unary-alphabet restriction; Translation III builds deterministic parity automata for FO2 using small-model representatives. FO2[LTL] inherits the maximum complexity of its components, while Let definitions make FO2[<] exponentially harder.

    - title: Model Checking Techniques for Verification of an Encryption Scheme for Wireless Sensor Networks
    - what: Presents a framework that models a hierarchical wireless-sensor-network encryption transmission as a Petri net, translates the net to Promela, and checks LTL correctness properties with SPIN. The example combines elliptic-curve encryption/decryption, LDPC encoding/decoding, modulation, fading/noise, and channel-parameter restoration. The paper gives a concrete Petri-net-to-Promela encoding: place and transition markings are integer arrays, firing macros atomically remove input tokens, add output tokens, and increment transition counts, and a BNF skeleton generates one init process with a do-loop of atomic firings. It explains SPIN never-claim generation from negated LTL, then defines deadlock-freeness as eventual firing of every transition and safeness as always keeping every place at ≤1 token. The communication model has 25 places and 14 transitions, including elliptic-curve/LDPC operations and a noisy fading channel. SPIN reports zero errors for the modeled liveness and safeness checks; the authors identify integrity/security properties as future work.

- Complete symmetry reduction in safety verification (2012)
    - title: A Complete Method for Symmetry Reduction in Safety Verification
    - what: Introduces a complete symmetry-reduction method for safety verification of finite, parametrically defined multi-process systems without precomputed global symmetry. It defines weak symmetry relative to the safety property, learns state interpolants backward over the interleaving tree, transforms interpolants by process permutations, and prunes states whose symmetric future is covered. The DFS algorithm handles cycles with fixpoint interpolation. Weak symmetry compares program-counter tuples, safety truth under a permutation, and bijective matching of enabled/scheduled transitions while deliberately ignoring shared-variable values; strong symmetry additionally requires full state equality. The algorithm memoizes interpolants per program point, recursively conjoins weakest-precondition approximations for enabled and disabled transitions, detects cycles and computes path-invariant fixpoints, then prunes if a permuted memoized interpolant holds. Theorem 1 proves pruning sound; Theorem 2 proves completeness with respect to weak symmetry when precondition computation is monotonic and symmetry preserving. Examples show pruning despite differing sums and process IDs.
    - number: 3.2 GHz processor, 2 GB memory, 5-minute timeout

    - number: reader-writer 8 readers/4 writers: CSR 3.23 s vs lazy 81,969 s

Correctness requires safety properties symmetric under the chosen permutation, and precondition computation must be both symmetry preserving and monotonic; weakest preconditions are expensive and practical approximations may not always satisfy these properties. The method targets safety, not arbitrary CTL*/liveness, and explores interleavings via DFS with memoized formulas.

- CSolve: Verifying C with Liquid Types (2012)
    - what: C memory-safety verifier combining physical heap-layout/pointer types with SMT-checked liquid refinement types. Infers predicates from a user/library qualifier vocabulary, generating subtyping constraints and solving them by predicate-abstraction fixed point. Demonstrates bounded string manipulation and recursive list-field invariants. Separates layout inference from bounds inference, explains modular checking of annotated library functions versus caller-driven inference, and tracks potential aliasing through named location parameters. Recursive list type ties each node’s string capacity to its length field using @offset expressions, allowing unbounded list contents to carry dependent bounds without individual-node enumeration.

This paper describes the architecture, not a new full soundness proof or independently checked compiler/solver implementation. §§1/2/3: refinement candidates are conjunctions of instantiated logical qualifiers from a supplied file plus standard library. Low annotation burden is the authors’ claim, conditional on adequate qualifiers/specifications; not annotation-free arbitrary invariant discovery. No completeness or success guarantee beyond this hypothesis space is shown. §3: CHECK_TYPE checks a function against its declared augmented type rather than inferring contract solely from uses. extern types are assumed for omitted bodies. A verified caller depends on those contracts and trusted malloc/library models; body omission is not proof of an external implementation. §3 pp.748–749: example relies on a malloc type yielding a non-NULL 12-byte allocated region, with no NULL check in printed caller. This is allocation-success/library-specification scope, not demonstrated handling of ISO C malloc failure. 12-byte structure and offsets 0/4/8 assume illustrated four-byte field/pointer layout; not a portable arbitrary-ABI theorem. §3: SAFE(p)=p>0 ∧ BS(p)≤p<BE(p); SIZE_GE(n) requires BE(p)−p≥n. STRINGPTR combines array shape with this pointer safety, not a proved zero-terminated string predicate. strntolower explicitly bounds accesses using n and short-circuit evaluation, so actual zero termination is not needed for the demonstrated bounds reasoning. §3: default nonaliasing assumption for separate function pointer arguments/returns is checked against bodies, and LOC/INST annotations describe may-alias sets. They permit possible aliases, not Rust-style unique ownership or proof that every member is the identical object. An omitted extern body’s stated alias contract remains assumed. §3: demonstration proves described access/type safety under the source model and contracts. It does not establish CSV parser functional correctness, list acyclicity, termination, leak freedom, deallocation/lifetime correctness or all ISO C undefined-behavior obligations. tolower is modeled as returning arbitrary char; text does not verify its standard argument-domain requirement. §3 p.749: full surrounding input routine omitted. The paper explicitly assumes inferred line/len types at call site before demonstrating propagated constraints. Do not claim an independently shown end-to-end verified input-reading implementation. §2: failed type checking may indicate physical/refinement type inability, with unsolved constraints; this is not a guaranteed concrete bug/counterexample. Multi-file makefile/drop-in GCC compatibility is a tool-interface claim, not proof of support for every GCC extension or arbitrary C program. Entire paper: no benchmark collection, timing, annotation counts, failure rates, hardware, solver-version details or comparative evaluation. No source artifact was run here. Detailed low-level liquid type theory is in cited POPL2010 work, not reproduced or counted as read.

- Hernandez localised security policies (2012)
    - title: Globally reasoning about localised security policies in distributed systems
    - what: Defines AspectKBL, a process-algebra language for distributed networks with security policies attached to locations, Belnap four-valued policy composition, labelled-transition semantics, and ACTL-like global safety obligations. It proposes checking each syntactic action directly instead of constructing the full LTS, yielding a safe over-approximation for finite systems. AspectKBL models parallel locations, tuple data, out/in/read actions, nondeterministic choice, and replicated processes; local aspects have pointcuts, applicability conditions, and four-valued recommendations. Policy-guarded transitions induce a pruned LTS. ACTLv obligations quantify over all paths and transitions matching a cut, checking predicates before/after interactions. The alternative checker unifies each action with an obligation cut, identifies source/target policies, collects recommendations as constraints, and certifies an action if policies deny it or their constraints imply the obligation predicate. It forbids replication to guarantee finite paths and avoid undecidable general model checking. Healthcare role/private-note examples and third-party-cookie models show both unsafe and policy-protected behavior. An Appendix gives a partial Haskell prototype; constraint solving, parser support, and a correctness proof remain incomplete.

- Lock Removal for Concurrent Trace Programs (2012)
    - what: Removes redundant lock statements from concrete concurrent trace programs while preserving shared-memory-access partial orders. This reduces constraints for later SMT-based predictive bug analysis. The method goes beyond removing purely thread-local locks by checking which locks maintain impossible control-state transitions. §2 shows a lock around only local operations can still restrict the order of surrounding shared accesses; naive removal introduces an assertion failure. §3 defines visible successors of global control states and a conservative static successor relation ignoring data. Theorem 1 says equality of these static successor sets before and after removal preserves partial orders of global operations. §4 summarizes each local path between adjacent shared accesses/lock acquisitions (pairs of interest) by a lock access pattern: initial/final held sets, backward/forward acquisition histories, continuously held locks and acquired locks. Inconsistent pattern pairs expose reachability barriers. Retaining at least one blocking lockset per barrier preserves impossible transitions; remaining locks can become nops. Pattern equivalence classes avoid enumerating all program-counter tuples. §5 iterates removal in the running example: B is first removed, then A becomes removable. Other synchronization can be ignored conservatively or incorporated through a universal causality graph.
    - number: 20 table traces, 1–21 threads, 55–45653 total events, up to 41 named locks; acquisition history nesting depths 0 or 1
    - number: BarrierB2: 13 threads, 805 events, 49 initial critical sections and 21 in transformed trace; removal 1.6 s, symbolic check 54.5→7.4 s

    - number: Elevator1: 184→174 critical sections; removal 0.1 s, check 29.6→0.7 s

Preservation concerns alternative interleavings of those fixed local paths, not all paths or whole-program source optimization. Static reachability overapproximates by ignoring shared-data consistency; extra synchronization can only reduce executions. The decomposition assumes nested locks and is incomplete beyond two threads. Experiments assume sequential consistency and use Yices. No proof for relaxed memory, fences, dynamic whole-program lock sets, general liveness, or arbitrary executions. The claimed linear worst-case local analysis should be read with the fixed-pattern/thread/lock assumptions; the algorithm explicitly compares inconsistent pattern combinations.     - title: Quantitative Synthesis for Concurrent Programs.
    - what: The paper synthesizes a deterministic finite-state concurrent program by resolving nondeterministic synchronization choices in a partial program. The synthesis problem reduces to imperfect-information stochastic graph games and is Nexp-complete; practical solving uses static strategy pruning, MDP strategy improvement, Gaussian elimination for Markov chains, and value-preserving data abstraction. A prototype handles producer-consumer, optimistic concurrency, and two other finite-state patterns. - Linear interfaces for parameterized model checking (2010)
    - title: Model-Checking Parameterized Concurrent Programs Using Linear Interfaces.
    - what: The paper introduces linear interfaces that summarize the effect of an arbitrary block of threads during k-round schedules of Boolean parameterized programs. A compositional fixed-point algorithm computes k-round reachability without enumerating all threads, and a two-player adequacy game checks whether states reachable at k+1 rounds are already reachable at k; if Adam wins, the program is proved correct for any thread count and schedule. The implementation uses symbolic BDDs/Getafix and evaluates predicate abstractions of Linux device drivers interacting with an OS kernel.

General reachability is undecidable; k-round exploration is an under-approximation. The adequacy game is sound but incomplete because Eve's one-thread-at-a-time declaration can give her spurious power. Detailed proofs are omitted from the conference paper and supplied in a cited full version.

    - title: Policy Monitoring in First-Order Temporal Logic.
    - what: Defines an effectively monitorable safety fragment of metric first-order temporal logic (MFOTL): formulas Ψ = □Ψ′ with bounded future temporal operators, arbitrary nesting of metric past and bounded future operators, quantifier alternation, and finite or automatic structures. An incremental monitor rewrites violations into a finite-relation fragment, maintains auxiliary relations for temporal subformulas, queues future obligations, and emits violating assignments online. The algorithm handles events and duration-like states by encoding starts/finishes, supports point-based metric timestamps, and incrementally updates past-since and bounded-future relations rather than recomputing windows. Four concrete policies formalize report approval and anti-money-laundering requirements (threshold reporting, authorization windows, and repeat-suspicious customers). The implementation’s steady-state analysis separates incremental time, mean/max auxiliary-relation space, and relevant active-domain size, exposing formula-structure effects (future operators can delay checks and inflate max space). Automatic structures are available in the broader work, while this paper evaluates finite relations.

The input language extends PRISM with unbounded-range variables, guarded commands and probabilistic updates. SMT enumeration builds BDD-encoded abstractions; reachability and goal pruning use forward/backward BDD analyses; sparse-matrix value iteration yields lower/upper probabilities and witness strategies. Parallel abstraction distinguishes program nondeterminism from abstraction nondeterminism and can tighten intervals. New features include reversed-DFS value-iteration order, interpolation bindings for MathSAT/CSIsat/FOCI, and on-the-fly layer-wise abstraction with incremental SMT solving.

    - title: SAT Based Bounded Model Checking with Partial Order Semantics for Timed Automata
    - what: Extends SAT-based bounded reachability checking for timed automata with multisteps that execute pairwise-independent transitions together. It defines synchronous, semi-synchronous and relaxed time-progress semantics, proves all are equivalent to ordinary timed runs, and implements the encodings in POEM with PicoSAT. The paper formalizes read/write independence, Mazurkiewicz equivalence and timed multisteps, proving via bubble-sort and extraction arguments that relaxed sequences can be reordered to normal-time runs and that all three multistep semantics preserve reachability. It gives SAT clauses for transition effects, dependency conflicts, value maintenance and timestamps, and explains how state invariants require local, reset-induced global and final-state checks. Experiments quantify clause/path-length tradeoffs: synchronous is compact, semi-synchronous often shortens paths, and relaxed can shorten paths further at encoding cost.

    - what: Defines a probabilistic model-checking procedure for infinite linear-time Propositional Projection Temporal Logic (PPTL) over discrete-time Markov chains by constructing an infinite-path normal-form graph, adding Rabin acceptance, determinizing it, and taking a product with the chain. The paper gives PPTL syntax and interval semantics, distinguishes finite and infinite normal-form paths, and removes finite paths to form NFG_inf. Its construction algorithm records self-loops and paired Rabin sets to exclude infinite repetition of strong chop; a Safra-style tree algorithm determinizes NFG_inf while merging equivalent PPTL formulas. The product construction labels accepting bottom strongly connected components and reduces formula probability to reachability of accepting BSCCs. A worked p;q chain yields an almost-sure result, illustrating the complete pipeline.

- Robust GR(1) liveness robustness (2010)
    - title: Robustness in the Presence of Liveness
    - what: Defines robustness for liveness specifications by requiring a minimum number of system guarantees to remain true as environment assumptions fail. It reduces single and multiple counting requirements to Generalized Reactivity (GR) objectives and gives verification and synthesis algorithms for robust systems. The paper develops concrete robustness measures using dining philosophers, formalizes them as ordered sets of GR(1)-like implications, and shows that disjunctions of conjunctions of Büchi objectives can be exponentially simplified to generalized Büchi objectives. It proves DCB game solving co-NP-complete via a 3SAT reduction, then gives a counter-based construction reducing GR(1) games to one-pair Streett games. The construction preserves winning strategies, extends to GR(k), and yields verification and synthesis complexity bounds; synthesized strategies trade lower runtime for larger memory than Zielonka’s method.

The model is reactive infinite-play games; liveness violations cannot be detected finitely, so safety guarantees cannot generally be sacrificed in response to a fairness-assumption violation. DCB-to-generalized-Büchi simplification is exponential and DCB game solving is co-NP-complete. The proposed GR(1) algorithm uses O(|S||E|(mn)^2) time but stores (m+1)(n+1) memory states (or n with an extra strategy computation); GR(k) incurs factorial/exponential factors.     - title: On the size of data structures used in symbolic model checking
    - what: Analyzes whether preprocessing the model or temporal formula can make model checking tractable and proves conditional lower bounds on symbolic state representations. The reductions establish k-arrow-PSPACE hardness/completeness even when one input part is preprocessed into polynomial space: interleaved model checking remains complete for full LTL and hard for the F fragment, while synchronous variants are hard. A separate state-membership problem shows that a polynomial-size BDD for legal initial states would collapse compilability classes; the argument extends to arbitrary decision diagrams whose evaluation lies in a polynomial-hierarchy level. Thus the worst-case blow-up is representation-independent under standard separation assumptions.

- Termination Analysis with Compositional Transition Invariants (2010)
    - what: Introduces Compositional Termination Analysis (CTA), replacing repeated expensive whole-program safety checks in Binary Reachability Analysis with ranking of loop-free unwindings and a transitivity check on a disjunctively well-founded candidate transition invariant. Increasing unwinding depth and removing already-ranked transitions permits short terminating fragments to yield a global termination argument. §2 defines transition invariants as supersets of transitive reachable transition closure, and disjunctive well-foundedness as finite unions of well-founded relations. §3 observes a transitive disjunctively well-founded relation is well-founded. Lemmas 1/2 accumulate rankings of increasingly deep, not-yet-covered unwindings and allow skipped intermediate depths; the implementation uses powers of two. Algorithm 1 tracks an overapproximation X of reachable states. A failed ranking produces a candidate nontermination precondition C: reachable C establishes nontermination; unreachable C is removed from X. Thus reachability checking remains where ranking fails rather than in every refinement. §4 slices each loop independently, havocs other loops and assignments depending on five or more variables, and uses CBMC symbolic execution to discover paths in loop-free fragments instead of enumerating all of them.
    - number: 87 drivers ×2 configurations =174 driver benchmarks
    - number: matched nontrivial successful BRA baseline: 99 terminating and 45 nonterminating cases
    - number: 3 GHz Xeon; 2 GB memory limit; 2 h per driver
    - number: precise CTA: average speedup 52; up to 3 orders of magnitude; more than 3× analyzed benchmarks at equal precision under the limit
    - limits: Soundness depends on the rank subprocedure returning a disjunctively well-founded superset or a genuine nontermination precondition, and on valid reachability checks. Finite-state nontermination completeness requires a complete rank procedure, unlike the implemented incomplete engine. Per-loop slicing/havoc overapproximates behavior and can lose termination proofs; practical heuristics replace assignments depending on at least five variables. Evaluations compare identical abstracted slices, not untouched drivers. Baseline is selected from BRA-successfully-analyzed, nontrivial loops, so speedup figures are conditional on that subset. Fast variants skip path-precondition checking or all reachability checking, potentially reporting false nontermination outside these benchmarks; the paper reports no precision loss on its measured examples. No scheduler fairness or busy-waiting progress argument is supplied for concurrent programs.

It uses checks for interference between threads, a step-merging technique called reduction, and permissions. Case studies include garbage collection, Paxos and locks.
    - limits: The test suite is a repository that keeps changing. It is not a fixed protocol benchmark. Pin a commit.

    - [source](https://civl-verifier.github.io/papers/fmcad2021.pdf); [notes: Civl and inductive sequentialization](../distributed_verification_review_b/deep_4_invariant_inference_benchmarks.md); [notes: S16](../distributed_verification_review_b/deep_9_formulation_methods.md)
